## v2026.11.01.1608 — F675-208 Member Expiry-Digest Receipt Provenance History (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle / authority:** Previous **Feature Improvement v1606** → Current **Feature Addition v1608** → Next **Feature Improvement v1610 (provisional)**. Latest main `1e389dc1a6b253f7dbff7cc6765fbe4a17bcb9e0` checked at start and midpoint against `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, English canonical and Korean equivalent master. This proposal is stacked on unmerged Draft #2335 (and predecessor #2328); developer issue #2342 / Draft PR #2343; F675-203–207 are **not implemented**. F675-208 is documentation only, no runtime/DB/WLD/ledger/Test/Production mutation.

### Purpose, source findings and design selection
- **Problem:** The proposed F675-205 09:00 KST daily in-app expiry digest has no member-visible, evidence-based answer to “Was an inbox notification actually created for my account on a particular day?” The current `frontend/src/app/account/notifications/page.tsx` is member-gated and has notification tabs and an unrelated engagement toggle, but no digest receipt history. `backend/src/notification/notification.controller.ts` already offers owner-guarded notification listing, search and read receipts; that inbox lists messages, not the atomic creation provenance of the proposed digest. The numbered `packages/database/migrations` and `init` directories contain **no verified canonical `in_app_notifications` CREATE TABLE definition** in this read; test fixtures do not establish deployable schema. No Production outage or missing live table is inferred.
- **Alternatives:** (A) infer “sent” from inbox search — rejected: deletion, retention, pagination and category changes make absence ambiguous; (B) create a new audit ledger/table — rejected: duplicate state and migration/retention burden; **(C) selected:** read the **existing proposed F675-205 unique (owner,KST-day) creation receipt and corresponding inbox row** in one read-only, owner-scoped database snapshot. This is a **creation-proof** panel, not delivery, read, job-success or finance proof. If F675-205 has not shipped, or receipt/inbox linkage is unverifiable, keep flag OFF and return 503; do not synthesize historical entries.

### Audience, permissions, entry, UI/CTA and states
- Authenticated and currently consented owner only. On `/account/notifications`, show “Expiry digest history — last 7 KST days”, **View history**, **Refresh**, **Open notification inbox**, and **Open inventory**. Explain: “Created means a notification was committed to your in-app inbox; it does not mean viewed or delivered to your device.” A missing receipt means **no verified creation record**, not “not sent”, “worker failed”, “missed” or “notifications disabled”. Never expose item names, quantities, balances, catalog IDs, raw receipt/notification IDs, owner UUIDs or other members' activity.
- Exactly seven `Asia/Seoul` calendar dates, newest first, including today, based on one PostgreSQL authoritative `asOfUtcMicros`; never client-local dates. State per date: `VERIFIED_CREATED` only when a unique owner/day receipt joins exactly one owner-matching notification in the same read snapshot; `WINDOW_OPEN` for **today from 09:00 through before 11:00 KST** when no verified creation exists (worker may still be processing; not evidence that it is running); `NOT_DUE` before 09:00 today; `NO_VERIFIED_RECORD` after the processing window or on previous days **only when authoritative receipt coverage for that date is proven** (still not proof no notification occurred); `NOT_TRACKED` on dates demonstrably before the tracking feature became active. Unknown coverage/activation watermark is 503, never a manufactured no-record. An orphan receipt, mismatched owner, duplicate day or missing referenced notification is **SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE 503** for the whole response, not a success-shaped “no record”. If historical receipts were pruned or the activation/coverage watermark cannot be verified, mark the entire seven-day history unavailable rather than silently infer absence.
- Page states: FLAG_OFF, LOADING, VERIFIED_WITH_CREATED, VERIFIED_WITHOUT_RECORD, REFRESHING, AUTH_REQUIRED 401, CONSENT_REQUIRED 403, RATE_LIMITED 429 with Retry-After, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE 503, OFFLINE, SESSION_CHANGED. Unknown/malformed timestamp or partial DB result never becomes a green badge. A verified response is a point-in-time observation; refresh re-reads. Existing notification search/tabs and engagement settings remain untouched.

### Exact API, data contract, DB constraints, transactions and indexes
- **Nest:** `GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/receipt-history`; no request body, actor UUID, date, arbitrary range, pagination or extra query parameters; reject extras with 400. Apply `SessionGuard`, `AuthenticatedGuard`, `ConsentGuard`, owner from trusted request only; no CSRF write token for read-only GET. `200 {sourceStatus:"VERIFIED",asOfUtcMicros:"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ",timezone:"Asia/Seoul",days:[{kstDate:"YYYY-MM-DD",state:"VERIFIED_CREATED"|"NOT_DUE"|"WINDOW_OPEN"|"NO_VERIFIED_RECORD"|"NOT_TRACKED",createdAtUtcMicros?:string}]}`. Exactly seven distinct dates; `createdAtUtcMicros` only for verified created. Strict response parsing: 401,403,429,503; invalid input 400. Do not return notification content or IDs. Backend and BFF must not map a 503 to empty history.
- **PostgreSQL (B):** a single read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction with one `statement_timestamp()` as-of, deterministic `Asia/Seoul` date boundaries, and an owner-scoped join from the **F675-205 daily claim/creation receipt** to the inbox notification; validate unique `(user_id,kst_date)`, receipt FK to an owner-matching notification and transactionally atomic receipt+notification creation before enabling. Existing F675-205 worker must not mark a receipt CREATED until the inbox row is committed in the same transaction. Proposed retention for both evidence sources **>=8 complete KST days** plus a verifiable tracking-activation/coverage watermark from existing audited feature-state metadata, subject to approved privacy/retention policy; if unavailable, return 503. No backfilling or inventing old receipts. Existing index `UNIQUE(user_id,kst_date)` and notification PK/owner key should support a seven-day bounded query; add an index only after `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS)` on realistic rows. No new table by default, no balances/holdings mutation, no worker reschedule.
- **Privilege boundary:** migrator-owned, fixed-search-path `SECURITY DEFINER` read function only if independently reviewed. `p_actor uuid` plus Nest authentication is **not independent database identity proof**; shared `moneyverse_app` EXECUTE with a forged UUID remains BLOCKED until the security owner proves binding or explicitly approves a weaker isolated-service trust model with documented controls. Revoke PUBLIC EXECUTE, no direct app-role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on member receipt, notification or `user_items` tables. Coordinate new migration numbering with the unresolved 318 conflict and production checksums; never rewrite applied migrations or assume fixture DDL is authoritative. Bound SQL timeout using transaction-local configuration, not persistent pooled-session SET.
- **Web/Android (A/C):** same-origin Next BFF `GET /api/shop/expiry-digest/receipt-history` using server-only `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`, strict upstream status/schema validation and `cache:'no-store'`; no `apiOrNull` false-empty fallback. Android `/app-api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/receipt-history` exact GET path only. Both success and every error/HEAD/conditional response must enforce `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; remove ETag, Last-Modified, Expires, 304 and upstream public caching at the actual edge. Abort/discard old account/session-generation responses on logout, consent withdrawal, account switch and newer refresh. No disk/offline cache or background replay.

### Security, admin, SEO, a11y, analytics, tests and rollout
- **Feature flag** `inventory_expiry_digest_receipt_history` default OFF and independently gated on F675-205 verified receipt+inbox schema and its delivery flag; turning history ON never enables digest delivery or changes a preference. Rate-limit GET to proposed <=10/member/minute with coarse global limits and bounded seven-row payload. Avoid recording owner UUID, notification content, receipt IDs, user item details or raw response in telemetry. No admin individual-member history or impersonation. Admin aggregate-only verified-created rate, unverified/no-record rate, 503 and mismatch counts, p95, stale-response drops, cohorts >=20 and suppression of low-count slices. This metric does **not** certify delivery success.
- Private route excluded from sitemap/canonical indexing; 320px layout, 200% zoom, >=44px touch controls, native time/date semantics, keyboard focus on refresh, screen-reader labels and polite aria-live without focus theft, reduced motion, Korean/English/Android parity, WCAG 2.2 AA. Proposed acceptance TARGETS (not observed): p95 <300ms for seven-day DB read, zero cross-owner disclosure, zero false VERIFIED_CREATED, zero ledger/item/WLD delta, zero cacheable owner responses.
- **QA acceptance NOT RUN:** fresh-install and upgrade PG17 schema/ACL/checksum parity; 10,001 holdings (no scan of holdings required), >=100 two-owner direct-role spoof and session-switch cases, >=100 mismatched/orphan/duplicate receipt+notification cases, KST 08:59:59.999999 / 09:00 / 10:59:59.999999 / 11:00 / 23:59:59.999999 and 7/8-day retention boundaries, worker/opt-out race, 401/403/429/503, malformed 200, HEAD/conditional/304 and cacheable upstream, Android offline/2-account, accessibility, no finance writes. Unit/mock-only CI is insufficient.
- **P0 (4):** OPS1608-01 prove actual Production executable SHA, independent rollback/restore, miniPC process-capacity gate; SEC1608-02 canonical notification DDL, owner receipt FK/uniqueness/retention, role ACL and spoof-negative, migration 318/checksum reconciliation; FIN1608-03 Treasury v1611 NOT_RECOVERED (552 Treasury events and 744 dividend records without verified provenance) and out-of-ledger crafting #2330 and fabricated stock trade toast #2340 — owned by B/C/QA, never paper over with notification receipts; REL1608-04 QA failures, official Test app/migrator DB identity #2260, Production locale #2262, full exact-SHA CI/Test and restore.
- **P1 (6):** DIGEST1608-05 B/DB owner-only seven-day query and EXPLAIN/negative ACL; DIGEST1608-06 B/Nest strict GET DTO and fail-closed mismatch handling; DIGEST1608-07 A/Next status card/BFF and accessible truthful copy; DIGEST1608-08 C/Android exact-path privacy and session fencing; DIGEST1608-09 A/C privacy headers, admin aggregate KPI, a11y and analytics; DIGEST1608-10 QA real PG17, worker/retention/KST and cross-owner tests, exact-SHA edge and rollback.
- **Release:** documentation DRAFT/HOLD; A/B/C/QA own separate branches, isolated test Docker, forward-only migrations and review. Gate: source exact SHA → full CI → official Test app/migrator exact SHA + real PG/API/web/Android acceptance → financial source reconciliation and independent restore → operator sign-off → OFF→staff→small cohort→broader rollout. Rollback switch OFF only; do not erase receipts or rewrite financial history. Main merge and Production promotion **NOT AUTHORIZED** by this planning. External independent reference new verified/deduplicated/classified **0**, cumulative **UNKNOWN / 10,000**, gate **BLOCKED / IN PROGRESS**.

## v2026.11.01.1606 — F675-207 Missing-Row, Claim-Day and Idempotency Hardening (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle and authority:** Previous **Feature Addition v1604** → Current **Feature Improvement v1606** → Next **Feature Addition v1608 (provisional)**. Latest main at start **9052076301bf1975422731ab50a8b7770dbbe951** and midpoint **1e389dc1a6b253f7dbff7cc6765fbe4a17bcb9e0** (Treasury runtime-identity v1609), reconciled into isolated v1606 worktree while preserving the unmerged v1604 proposal, issue **#2327** and Draft **#2328**. Authority: main AGENTS.md, README.md, English PROJECT_PLAN.md and Korean parity. F675-203–207 are **NOT IMPLEMENTED**. This is a documentation-only correction, not an observed incident, DB migration, permission grant, app change or deployment.

### Source-verified gaps and selected corrections

**D1 — An absent preference row cannot be locked with SELECT FOR UPDATE (P0 design defect).** v1604 proposes a verified absent row as default OFF/72h/revision 0, yet claims the worker and preference PUT serialize by locking that same row. If it does not exist, a row lock cannot serialize first-save, first opt-in, first daily claim and consent withdrawal. The real notification settings page at frontend/src/app/account/notifications/page.tsx has only an unrelated engagement toggle; no F675 preference endpoint, UI or table exists in current main. **Decision:** use a transaction-scoped, namespaced per-member advisory lock for **every** preference GET requiring claim-state consistency, PUT, opt-in/opt-out, worker claim and consent-revocation path, even when no preference row exists; then lock the actual row FOR UPDATE if present. The worker must not silently fall back to a weaker uncoordinated lock. For high-volume GET, either use a consistent read under that lock or explicitly label claim status as best-effort, never a linearizable guarantee. Do not hold a lock across network calls. When the consent subsystem cannot participate in the same owner serialization and verified consent recheck, delivery stays OFF/BLOCKED.

**D2 — Lock order, no-op and first-write CAS (P0).** PUT order: authenticate and validate strict payload → transaction-local idempotency-key advisory lock → read globally unique key receipt and verify owner plus canonical payload hash → acquire owner advisory lock → read/lock or create the single F675-205 preference row → recheck consent/feature flag → compare expected revision → change only lookahead_hours or return verified no-change → write immutable receipt → commit. Worker/opt-in/disable/revocation acquire owner lock first and never acquire the PUT key lock; this avoids a key/owner inversion. An absent row has verified revision 0, enabled false, lookahead 72; two first writes with expected 0 must yield one committed revision 1 and one 409, never duplicate preference rows. Saving 72 on an absent row may remain a verified no-op at revision 0, but the receipt must explicitly record that no preference row was created; it cannot imply digest opt-in. Revision overflow, malformed decimal, null, array, unknown field and stale revision fail closed. PostgreSQL session SET is prohibited for pooled timeout settings; use SET LOCAL inside a transaction or a reviewed dedicated role/pool.

**D3 — Idempotency replay must not masquerade as current settings (P1).** A receipt keyed only by (user_id, idempotency_key) permits the same UUID to be accepted independently for another owner. Prefer global UNIQUE(idempotency_key) with stored owner, canonical request hash, original outcome, original revision and created_at; cross-owner or mismatched-payload reuse returns generic 409 without disclosing the other owner. Same-key retry while original revision remains current may return 200 REPLAYED with the original committed result. If a later preference update/disable changed the current revision or opt-in state, replay returns 409 REPLAYED_STALE and requires a fresh GET, never a stale 200 falsely labeled current. A proposed seven-day receipt retention is a **bounded replay window**, not lifetime exactly-once semantics; expired-key retries must still obey current revision CAS, with no destructive cleanup of immutable audit evidence. Hash excludes untrusted headers and uses normalized 24/72 integer plus expected revision and operation type.

**D4 — Today versus next digest is a lower bound, not a delivery promise (P1).** The old effectiveFromKstDate field is misleading if a worker claims after the API response. Replace it in the proposed (not deployed) contract with earliestPossibleKstDate and claimObservation {kstDate,claimedAtUtcMicros|null,observedAtUtcMicros}, explicitly a snapshot rather than a guarantee. PostgreSQL is authoritative for Asia/Seoul day and one UTC six-digit fractional as-of. If today's unique (user_id,kst_date) claim exists at the serialization point, a save cannot change it; the earliest possible application is the next KST day. Otherwise it can affect today's not-yet-claimed digest, subject to opt-in, consent, inventory and worker availability. Worker snapshot includes enabled, 24/72 selection, revision, consent and claim day in one transaction; the notification and unique daily receipt commit atomically. Zero eligible holdings produce no success-shaped delivery claim. At 08:59:59.999999, 09:00:00, 10:59:59.999999, 11:00:00, 23:59:59.999999 KST and DST-independent UTC conversions, assert exact inclusion boundaries. A successful preference save **never** turns enabled ON or changes WLD/item/ledger balances.

### Exact cross-platform handoff, security, analytics and acceptance

- **API/DB (B):** Keep GET/PUT /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preferences, strict actor-from-session SessionGuard/AuthenticatedGuard/ConsentGuard and PUT CsrfGuard; no actor override. GET 200 verified OFF/72/revision 0 only after a real successful DB read; DB/schema/consent uncertainty is 403/503, not default 0. PUT body remains {lookaheadHours:24|72,expectedRevision:canonical decimal,idempotencyKey:UUID}; return UPDATED, VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE or current REPLAYED, and 409 STALE_REVISION/KEY_REUSE_CONFLICT/REPLAYED_STALE. Ensure the service trust-boundary decision for SECURITY DEFINER actor UUID is explicitly approved; shared app-role direct cross-owner spoof remains a **BLOCKED** grant gate (#993). Never grant direct user_items or notification table DML to fix an endpoint. Use one existing F675-205 preference table, UNIQUE owner/day claim and globally unique idempotency receipt; reconcile migration 318 collision (#2233), schema/checksums and clean install before new SQL.
- **Web (A):** Existing server-only frontend/src/lib/api.ts cannot be imported into a client component. Proposed same-origin frontend/src/app/api/shop/expiry-digest/preferences/route.ts validates exact JSON and propagates 401/403/409/429/503; client radio/Save/Preview/Open inventory must display verified revision and **earliest possible** day, not “scheduled” or “sent”. Disable Save on unknown revision; AbortController and request/session generation discard late responses after account switch, logout, consent withdrawal or conflict. Keep separate existing goal-notification setting unchanged; no apiOrNull success-shaped fallback.
- **Android/app-api (C):** Exact shop/expiry-digest/preferences path and method matching, no broad public-shop cache change. The current app-api proxy forwards selected upstream response headers and private-overrides only selected families, not this proposed path; force private/no-store, noindex/nofollow, no-referrer, nosniff and strip ETag/Last-Modified/Expires/304 on success **and** error/HEAD/conditional requests at the final edge. No Android disk caching or offline save queue; two-account and replay isolation mandatory.
- **Admin/security/SEO/a11y:** Feature inventory_expiry_digest_lookahead defaults OFF independently of F675-205 delivery flag. Admin can only audit flag changes with reauthentication and see aggregate settings/claim conflicts for cohorts >=20; no member impersonation, raw UUID, item details or receipt body in logs. Member routes are force-dynamic/noindex/nofollow and excluded from sitemap. 320px, 200% zoom, >=44px controls, native fieldset/radio, keyboard, focus, aria-live, reduced motion and Korean/English/Android screen-reader parity. Proposed p95 GET/PUT <300/500ms, zero duplicate digest/day, zero cross-owner reads, zero false-default on error and zero cacheable owner responses are **TEST TARGETS, NOT OBSERVED**.
- **Real acceptance required (NOT RUN):** PostgreSQL 17 fresh-install+upgrade and migration/checksum/ACL parity; absent-row concurrent first-save/first-opt-in/worker/disable with 100 interleavings, two-member direct-role spoof-negative and global-key collision tests, same-key 100 retries, mismatched payload, stale replay after a later revision, 7-day retention boundary, rev=0/max and overflow, consent withdrawal during claim, daily claim at KST boundaries, microsecond 24h/72h expiry counts over 10,001 holdings, SQL timeout and pooled connection reuse, 401/403/409/429/503/HEAD/304/cacheable upstream, browser/Android account switch, accessibility, and zero item/WLD/ledger delta. No unit/mock-only pass is an exact-SHA Test acceptance.
- **P0 backlog (4):** OPS1606-01 Production executable SHA/rollback/independent restore and miniPC cgroup EAGAIN #2171; SEC1606-02 absent-row owner lock and consent/DB trust boundary, DEV app-role grants #993, migration-318/checksum drift; FIN1606-03 ledger provenance and zero financial writes, Treasury v1611 NOT_RECOVERED with 552 unlinked historical events and 744 dividends (read-only RCA), plus newly reported **out-of-band crafting_execute** direct cash/inventory mutation without ledger #2330 (separate B v723/C v1262/QA ownership; no duplicate code edits); REL1606-04 Test app/migrator target mismatch #2260, exact-SHA gate #1088, Production release-identity mismatch and locale #2262, Treasury v1611 postreset RCA.
- **P1 backlog (6):** DIGEST1606-05 (B/DB) owner-lock + absent-row/receipt schema and EXPLAIN; DIGEST1606-06 (B/API) strict CAS/replay/current-state response and consent fencing; DIGEST1606-07 (A) verified web state machine and nonpromissory claim-day copy; DIGEST1606-08 (C) Android exact-path privacy and session/replay fence; DIGEST1606-09 (A/C) private SEO, admin aggregate KPI and WCAG parity; DIGEST1606-10 (QA) real PG17 concurrency, negative role tests, KST boundary, edge headers, finance zero-delta and rollback.
- **Release/rollback:** Documentation Draft/HOLD only. B/A/C/QA implement on their own branches and isolated Test containers, never in this planning run. Exact source SHA → full CI → official Test app/migrator identity + authenticated PG/API/web/Android acceptance → independent backup restore and financial reconciliation → operator approval → staged feature flag OFF→canary→broader Production. On any mismatch keep OFF; roll back flag/route without destructive migration or rewriting financial history. Latest QA #2330 is a **reported source/DEV risk**, not proven Production crafting loss. External independent references newly verified/deduplicated/classified **0**, cumulative **UNKNOWN / 10,000** → **BLOCKED / IN PROGRESS**.

## v2026.11.01.1604 — F675-207 Member Expiry Digest Lookahead Preference (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle / authority:** Previous **Feature Improvement v1602** → Current **Feature Addition v1604** → Next **Feature Improvement v1606 (provisional)**. Main at start `143190d3811a1a419bfdfb2bab968e34fee447df`; at mid-run `95877554097b595d8dcfa28b60ecb65e50bf0c2d` after Treasury v1607 merge; latest main AGENTS.md, README.md, English PROJECT_PLAN.md (canonical), and Korean parity are authority. This documentation branch preserves unmerged Draft **#2315** without overwriting latest-main ops files. F675-203–207 are **PROPOSALS, NOT IMPLEMENTED**. No runtime, DB, WLD, ledger, Test or Production mutation.

### Goal, audience, source evidence, alternatives
- **F675-207 goal:** an authenticated, consent-current member who opted into proposed F675-205 daily in-app expiry digest may choose a **24-hour** or **72-hour** lookahead; 72 hours is the default for an unset preference. This controls which held-item expiry bands the **next eligible** daily digest includes, not the 09:00 KST dispatch time, financial settlement, item expiration, or notification permissions. The preference may be saved while digest delivery is OFF, but **must never turn delivery ON**. F675-206 preview remains a read-only point-in-time estimate and can display both bands with the selected band highlighted; it never creates a delivery receipt.
- **Observed code:** `frontend/src/app/account/notifications/page.tsx` has a member-gated server component and a separate goal-notification setting, but no expiry lookahead; `backend/src/notification/notification.controller.ts` has session/auth/consent and CSRF on writes; `packages/database/migrations/071-shop-catalog-schema.sql` stores held `user_items.expires_at`; `frontend/src/lib/app-gateway.ts` admits the shop group but does not prove an exact private response policy for a new preference endpoint. Latest main also includes QA dual-disk changes #2321/#2324. The unmerged QA #2326 reports client-side fabricated mini-showdown WLD success; **not a verified wallet mutation**. These are source observations, not proof of deployed F675 behavior.
- **Alternatives:** A) hardcode 72 hours forever (no user control); B) browser-only preference (cross-device inconsistency and worker cannot trust it); **C) selected:** a versioned server preference reused by the F675-205 worker and F675-206 UI. Do not introduce a separate preference store if F675-205 has already created one. No new distributed planning document.

### Member journey, permissions, states, and UI contract
- **Entry:** authenticated `/account/notifications`, section "Inventory expiry digest" under the existing notification preferences. Show current delivery opt-in status separately. Radio choices **Next 24 hours** / **Next 72 hours**; CTA **Save lookahead**; secondary **Preview now** and **Open inventory**. Show "Applies to the next digest not yet claimed; this does not enable notifications." Initial default 72 hours when a verified database read finds no preference; never infer a verified default from a failed request.
- **States:** FLAG_OFF (old page unchanged), LOADING, VERIFIED_DEFAULT_OFF, VERIFIED_SAVED_OFF, VERIFIED_SAVED_ON, SAVING, VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE, STALE_REVISION (409, refetch without overwriting), AUTH_REQUIRED (401), CONSENT_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429 with Retry-After), SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (503), SESSION_CHANGED and OFFLINE. An error must not render a success toast, a default, or a digest opt-in. Save is disabled while the verified revision is unavailable. Show explicit saved revision and next eligible KST date when known; no misleading promise of delivery.
- **Time rule:** 09:00 KST daily F675-205 worker remains the sole delivery authority; local day is `Asia/Seoul` not UTC. If a worker has already claimed the member/day, the new preference applies no earlier than the next local day. Otherwise the committed preference may apply to that day's claim. The worker must snapshot `enabled`, `lookahead_hours`, revision, and claim day atomically under the same member-preference row lock before creating the daily notification + unique receipt. One notification maximum per member/KST day, regardless of retries or preference changes.

### API, schema, transactions, security and privacy (implementation handoff only)
- **Nest API:** `GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preferences` and `PUT /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preferences`. Both require SessionGuard, AuthenticatedGuard, ConsentGuard; PUT additionally CsrfGuard, strict JSON, same-origin protections and per-member rate limits. Actor always derives from the verified session, never body/query/header. Reject unknown fields and query params. GET 200 `{sourceStatus:"VERIFIED",enabled:false,lookaheadHours:72,revision:"0",effectiveFromKstDate:"YYYY-MM-DD"}` for a verified absent row; a saved row returns its actual enabled/revision. PUT body `{lookaheadHours:24|72,expectedRevision:"<canonical nonnegative decimal>",idempotencyKey:"<uuid>"}` changes **only lookaheadHours**, not enabled. PUT 200 returns the same verified shape and `result:"UPDATED"|"VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE"|"REPLAYED"`; 400 malformed, 401 unauthenticated, 403 consent/owner, 409 stale revision or mismatched-key replay, 429 throttled, 503 unknown DB/worker authority. Never return 0/default on upstream failure.
- **Web transport:** server-only `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` must stay server-only. A narrow same-origin Next BFF at `/api/shop/expiry-digest/preferences` forwards GET/PUT using the existing authenticated server transport, validates upstream content type/shape, and propagates fail-closed errors. Client island uses `cache:'no-store'`, AbortController, monotonically increasing request/session generation and revision CAS; discard responses after logout, account switch, consent withdrawal, stale save or newer refresh. No `apiOrNull` success-shaped fallback.
- **Android/app-api:** exact-path `shop/expiry-digest/preferences` GET/PUT parity, authenticated session + CSRF-equivalent write protections; force `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on success/error/HEAD. Strip ETag, Last-Modified, Expires and conditional validators; never return 304 for owner state. Prove two-account isolation and no replay across session generations. Do not change public shop caching.
- **DB:** extend the **single** F675-205 preference record, if/when implemented: `user_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id)`, `enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, `lookahead_hours smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 72 CHECK (lookahead_hours IN (24,72))`, `revision bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (revision>=0)`, `updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL`; preserve existing opt-in/consent metadata and never silently migrate enabled to true. A distinct receipt store keyed `(user_id,idempotency_key)` records canonical request hash, outcome and revision; uniqueness plus 7-day bounded retention (policy and replay window reviewed) is a **proposal**, not a deployed schema. Index `user_id` PK; add an `enabled=true` worker index only after EXPLAIN on realistic cohorts. Migration sequence currently reaches 317 on main; reconcile outstanding 318 conflict #2233 and Production checksums before allocating any new number.
- **Transaction ordering:** PUT validates → advisory lock on **idempotency key** → receipt lookup/owner and payload hash verification → member preference row lock → expected revision CAS → update or verified no-op → receipt insert → commit; same-key concurrent requests replay exactly one committed result, mismatched payload fails. Worker obtains the **same preference row lock**, snapshots lookahead and enabled, then inserts the member/KST-day unique delivery receipt and inbox row in one transaction. Disable/consent withdrawal races must be tested; if revoked before worker snapshot, suppress delivery. Failure must not produce an orphan notification, a receipt without a notification, or a false "sent" status. PostgreSQL timeout uses transaction-local scope only, never a pooled persistent SET.
- **P0 identity boundary:** a SECURITY DEFINER function accepting `p_actor uuid` does **not** independently authenticate a member. No direct app-role EXECUTE/SELECT grant until the security owner proves a genuine DB identity boundary or documents an explicitly approved weaker service-trust model with compensating controls; two-member direct-role spoof-negative test required. Revoke PUBLIC, avoid table-wide DML grants (#993), CSRF/session-fixation/IDOR tests, cap PUT 5/min and GET 30/min per owner (test targets), reject duplicate keys, enforce resource/size bounds. No owner UUID, token, item details, or raw preference payload in logs; audit only coarse outcome and revision. No WLD/item/ledger writes.

### Admin, SEO, accessibility, analytics, QA, release
- **Admin:** feature flag `inventory_expiry_digest_lookahead` defaults **OFF**, separate from F675-205 delivery flag. Admin may inspect aggregate setting-change and claim-conflict counts, but cannot impersonate a member or silently opt them in. Audit flag changes with privileged reauthentication; emergency OFF hides CTA without deleting saved choices. Use cohort >=20 for aggregate dashboards and suppress low-count slices.
- **SEO/mobile/a11y:** member-only dynamic noindex/nofollow, never sitemap/canonical public listing; 320px viewport, 200% zoom, >=44px touch targets, native radio group/fieldset, keyboard/focus, descriptive save errors, `aria-live` non-duplicative announcements, reduced motion, Korean/English strings and Android screen-reader parity. Preference is accessible offline only as clearly stale local display; no offline save queue.
- **KPI (PROPOSED TARGETS, NOT OBSERVED):** verified GET success and false-default rate (target 0), saved preference adoption, 24h/72h selection share, opt-in unchanged after save (target 100%), worker preference-to-receipt consistency (target 100%), duplicate digest/day (target 0), cross-owner access (target 0), response cache violations (target 0), p95 GET/PUT <300/500ms, conflict/429/503 and retry rates; privacy-safe cohort aggregates only.

## v2026.11.01.1602 — F675-206 Expiry Digest Preview Transport, Privacy and Trust-Boundary Hardening (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle / authority:** Previous **Feature Addition v1600** → Current **Feature Improvement v1602** → Next **Feature Addition v1604 (provisional)**. Canonical origin/main `f13bbce273ffc65e8576170992d82ea00c27a1c9` rechecked; read AGENTS.md, README.md, PROJECT_PLAN.md (English authority) and PROJECT_PLAN.ko.md. Stacked on unmerged documentation Draft **#2309**; handoff **#2307**. F675-203/205/206 are **NOT IMPLEMENTED**. No new feature, migration, SQL grant, API, UI, inbox write or runtime deployment in this planning cycle.

### Source-verified gaps and decisions

**D1 — Web preview has no specified browser transport (P1).** `frontend/src/app/account/notifications/page.tsx` is a server component guarded by `requireMember()` and uses `apiOrNull()` for the unrelated engagement preference. `apiOrNull()` deliberately maps API errors to null; it cannot be used to prove a zero count. The proposed Nest `GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preview` is not directly callable from a client island through the server-only `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`. **Decision:** Dev A owns a narrow same-origin **GET `/api/shop/expiry-digest/preview`** Next route at `frontend/src/app/api/shop/expiry-digest/preview/route.ts`, forwarding the current request's session through the existing server-side API helper, with explicit typed `ApiError` propagation (401/403/429; all unverified upstream/parse/clock errors 503). No fallback `[]`, `null`, `0`, success-shaped mock, anonymous cached result, CSRF write, opt-in or notification creation. A client-only `expiry-digest-preview-panel.tsx` is embedded under the existing notification settings; it fetches this BFF with `cache:'no-store'`, validates `sourceStatus==='VERIFIED'`, canonical nonnegative decimal strings and a real UTC microsecond timestamp, and distinguishes VERIFIED_ZERO from SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. BFF and client tests must prove upstream 200 malformed JSON/HTML/null never becomes a verified count.

**D2 — Android gateway can inherit cacheable upstream shop headers (P0 privacy gate).** `frontend/src/lib/app-gateway.ts:48-74` admits the `shop` group, while `frontend/src/app/app-api/v1/[...path]/route.ts:501-513` copies upstream headers and forces private/noindex only for `shop/purchases`, not `shop/expiry-digest/preview`. `handle()` around lines 565-603 also lacks an exact preview override. **Decision:** Dev C must match only `['shop','expiry-digest','preview']`, require GET (HEAD handled explicitly without a reusable cached entity), validate the exact success payload before passing it to Android, and force `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on 200, 400, 401, 403, 405, 429, 503, 502/504 and malformed upstream 200. Strip `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `Expires` and cache validators; reject or ignore conditional request validators so 304 cannot authenticate an old member's response. Do not change public `shop/items` and `shop/public-catalog` caching by broad group matching. Validate the final edge (including CDN/proxy) and Android account-switch isolation; source risk is **not proof of a Production disclosure**.

**D3 — A verified read is not indefinitely current (P1).** A six-digit PostgreSQL `statement_timestamp()` describes the read, not the display time. On receipt show “verified at” and use a monotonic UI timer: after **60 seconds** mark the panel STALE and require an explicit Refresh to claim current counts; when returning from a hidden tab or offline state, do not silently relabel old values VERIFIED. Keep the old value only with a visible stale label, never as an active zero. Use `AbortController` plus monotonically increasing request/session generations to discard late responses after refresh, logout, consent withdrawal or account change. Never use client `Date` to determine the two expiry windows; SQL owns `(asOf,asOf+24h]` and `(asOf+24h,asOf+72h]`. A slow response or unparseable `asOfUtcMicros` must be unavailable, not verified. 60 seconds is a **proposed UX policy**, not a measured freshness SLA.

**D4 — Actor UUID is not a database identity, and timeout settings can leak across a pool (P0 security gate).** `packages/database/migrations/071-shop-catalog-schema.sql:14-16` defines `user_items` PK `(user_id,catalog_id)` with `quantity>=0` and `expires_at timestamptz`, revoking app table access; migration 123's `shop_my_items_v2(p_actor uuid)` is a `SECURITY DEFINER` function that trusts the supplied actor. An app principal with direct EXECUTE on a new `shop_expiry_digest_preview_v1(p_actor uuid)` can supply another valid UUID: a Nest guard alone cannot make a direct app-role spoof-negative test pass. **Decision:** do **not** grant that function to the shared app principal until the security owner chooses and proves a real identity-bound database boundary (e.g. independently authenticated per-principal execution), or explicitly documents and accepts the weaker service-trust model with separate credentials and compensating controls; do not mislabel service checks or a writable GUC as independent DB proof. In either model prohibit direct `user_items` SELECT, require two-owner cross-actor negative tests and revoke PUBLIC. The proposed 2s SQL budget must be enforced without persistent session `SET` on pooled connections: use a verified per-transaction `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` inside READ ONLY transaction or a safely configured dedicated pool/role, with timeout and pool-reuse regression. The aggregate uses a single SQL statement/snapshot, owner predicate, `quantity>0`, nonnull `expires_at`, and exact microsecond bounds; count one PK catalog row once, not total quantity or `effect_expires_at`. Use EXPLAIN on 10,001 synthetic holdings before considering `(user_id,expires_at)` index; 10 requests/owner/minute plus coarse abuse protection and 429 Retry-After are **test targets**.

### Exact implementation handoff, acceptance and release

- **API/DB:** Nest owner-only guarded GET with strict empty-query contract, actor derived from verified session, 200 `{sourceStatus:'VERIFIED',asOfUtcMicros:'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ',count0To24h:'0',count24To72h:'0'}`; 401/403/429/503. No body/actor override, no write or receipt. No DB identity claim until P0 security signoff. `shop_my_items_v2` uses separate `clock_timestamp()` checks, so **do not** use its returned array as an atomic count oracle; compare against a direct single-asOf SQL reference in isolated PG17. New migration only after conflicting sequence 318 is reconciled.
- **User/UI/SEO:** authenticated owner only at `/account/notifications`; Preview / Refresh / Open inventory; OFF flag preserves old page; 320px, 200% zoom, 44px touch, keyboard, `aria-live`, reduced motion, KO/EN parity and WCAG 2.2 AA. Preview does not enable F675-205 or guarantee 09:00 KST delivery. All success/errors and HEAD at BFF, Nest, app-api, edge private/no-store/noindex; no sitemap, public canonical, owner IDs, item data or raw response in logs.
- **Admin/KPI:** attempts, verified-zero, stale-rate, invalid payload, 401/403/429/503, p95, dropped stale-session responses, cross-owner attempts; aggregate only for cohorts >=20, no individual activity dashboard. p95 <300ms and zero cacheable owner responses are acceptance **targets**, not measurements.
- **QA (PROPOSED, NOT RUN):** PG17 clean-install + upgrade, 2 owners/100 spoof attempts, 10,001 holdings, 1µs boundaries, 100 concurrent read/write cases, clock/timeout/pool reuse, 200 malformed/HTML/null, 401/403/429/503/502/504, HEAD/304/conditional validators, malicious upstream `Cache-Control: public` + ETag, CDN response headers, stale tab/late responses/logout/consent withdrawal, Android two-account cache isolation, a11y, and zero item/WLD/ledger mutations. ## v2026.11.01.1600 — F675-206 Member Inventory Expiry Digest Read-only Preview (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle / authority:** Previous **Feature Improvement v1598** → Current **Feature Addition v1600** → Next **Feature Improvement v1602 (provisional)**. Canonical origin/main `f13bbce273ffc65e8576170992d82ea00c27a1c9` verified at start and midpoint; read main AGENTS.md, README.md, PROJECT_PLAN.md (English authority), and PROJECT_PLAN.ko.md. Previous planning Draft **#2301** is OPEN/unmerged and its valid F675-199–205 designs are carried forward in this isolated documentation branch. Developer handoff **#2307**, Draft PR **#2309**. **F675-206 is not implemented.** No distributed feature-plan file or runtime deployment.

### Source evidence, user value, alternatives
- **Verified source:** `frontend/src/app/account/notifications/page.tsx` already has a member-gated notification settings page and a separate existing goal-notification preference; it does not provide an expiry preview. `frontend/src/app/inventory/page.tsx` calls `apiOrNull('/api/v1/shop/holdings')` then converts missing data to `[]`, so it cannot establish verified zero when the upstream fails. `backend/src/shop/shop.controller.ts` guards GET holdings with Session/Authenticated/Consent guards; `shop.repository.ts` reads `public.shop_my_items_v2(actor)` from migration 123. `frontend/src/app/app-api/v1/[...path]/route.ts` explicitly protects selected private families but not every shop/holdings path. These are source findings, not proof of a Production privacy incident.
- **Goal:** let an authenticated, consent-current owner see what a **hypothetical** daily expiry digest would count **now**, before deciding whether to enable F675-205. Existing F675-203 urgency summary and F675-205 worker are unimplemented proposals; this feature must not claim their rollout, send a notification, save a preference, or create an inbox receipt.
- **Alternatives:** (A) reuse the full unbounded holdings payload in the browser: rejected (false-empty, scale, client-clock precision); (B) persist a preview snapshot: rejected (stale data, retention and consent burden); **(C) selected:** a bounded owner-scoped PostgreSQL read aggregate behind a typed Nest GET. If F675-203's aggregate is already implemented at development time, reuse that verified authoritative query rather than create duplicate counting logic. No new table or financial write.

### Member flow, UI and exact response
- **Entry:** `/account/notifications`, below the proposed daily expiry digest preference. CTA **Preview expiry digest** → **Refresh preview** → **Open inventory**. Preview works with digest preference OFF and does **not** opt the user in. Explain: “Current inventory estimate only. Counts can change; scheduled notifications are not guaranteed.” Show the two bands, source timestamp and last verified refresh; no item names, catalog IDs, balances, quantities, raw owner IDs or simulated inbox messages.
- **Bands:** one PostgreSQL `statement_timestamp()` `asOf` in UTC, precision six fractional digits. Distinct catalog kinds in **(asOf, asOf+24 hours]** and **(asOf+24 hours, asOf+72 hours]**, including `quantity>0` and nonnull held-item `expires_at` only. Exclude already expired, `effect_expires_at`, upkeep, suspended-status inference and ledger/financial events. One `user_items` PK (owner,catalog) row counts once per band. Counts are **canonical nonnegative decimal strings**, not JS floating numbers. Boundary examples: expires exactly at asOf → excluded; exactly at +24h → first band; +24h+1µs → second; exactly +72h → second; +72h+1µs → excluded.
- **States:** FLAG_OFF (existing page unchanged), LOADING, VERIFIED_NONZERO, VERIFIED_ZERO, REFRESHING, AUTH_REQUIRED, CONSENT_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, OFFLINE and SESSION_CHANGED. A 503/timeout/unknown timestamp must never become zero or a “no expiry” success badge. A verified preview is a point-in-time read, **not** a frozen future digest or a guarantee that the 09:00 worker will run. Expired session/account switch clears the panel, not just its spinner.

### API, DB authority, privacy, abuse and performance
- **Nest:** proposed `GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preview` with SessionGuard + AuthenticatedGuard + ConsentGuard and actor derived solely from the authenticated request. No actor UUID, filter or body accepted; unexpected query parameters → 400; no CSRF write token or idempotency key for GET. `200 {sourceStatus:'VERIFIED',asOfUtcMicros:'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ',count0To24h:'0',count24To72h:'0'}`. 401 unauthenticated, 403 consent, 429 rate limited, 503 DB/schema/clock unknown. Retry is a fresh read, never a replay of a previous success.
- **SQL:** forward-only migration only if required, with numbering coordinated after competing migration **318**; proposed `public.shop_expiry_digest_preview_v1(p_actor uuid)` SECURITY DEFINER, migrator-owned, fixed `search_path=pg_catalog,pg_temp`, schema-qualified tables, explicit PUBLIC EXECUTE revoke and reviewed role-specific EXECUTE. One read-only statement, owner predicate inside SQL, strict microsecond comparator, no dynamic SQL. **P0 security gate:** an actor UUID argument and caller-writable session GUC are not independent DB identity proof. Demonstrate effective app-role negative table grants and two-owner direct EXECUTE spoof-negative tests, or block the new grant/feature until a reviewed identity-bound function boundary exists. Do not grant direct `user_items` SELECT or notification-table rights to make preview work.
- **Resource limits:** proposed 10 requests/member/minute, 2s SQL timeout and p95 <300ms **TEST TARGETS, not measurements**. Use `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on 10,001 synthetic holdings and review existing owner/expiry indexes; add an index only with measured benefit and no redundant duplicate. PostgreSQL one-statement snapshot and timestamp, no cross-request snapshot claim, no write transaction/locks/receipt. No dependency on unproven `in_app_notifications` DDL (that is F675-205's separate P0 blocker).
- **Privacy/SEO:** HTTP success **and errors** at Nest, Next BFF, app-api and public edge must return `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; no sitemap or public canonical for private preview. No member UUID, item/expiry detail, raw query, response payload or auth token in logs/analytics. Android app-api parity, no disk cache, cancel/discard stale responses on logout/account switch; 320px, 200% zoom, 44px touch targets, keyboard labels/aria-live, reduced motion, WCAG 2.2 AA, KO/EN meaning parity.
- **Admin/KPI:** aggregate-only preview attempts, verified-zero share, 401/403/429/503, p95 and stale-session response drops; suppress cohorts <20 distinct members. Targets: zero cross-owner disclosure, zero item/WLD/ledger mutations, zero false-empty on upstream failure, zero public-cache responses. No per-user preview dashboard, no external notification and no marketing inference.

### P0/P1 development backlog — 4 P0 + 6 P1 (OPEN)

2. **P0 SEC1600-02:** PG17 clean-install and upgrade parity, app-role ACL and cross-owner direct-EXECUTE spoof-negative; reconcile nine Production-only tables/five source references (#2242), five checksums, migration-318 collision (#2233), broad DEV app grants (#993). Block new grants until proof.

6. **P1 PREVIEW1600-06 (B/API):** guarded typed GET, strict decimal strings/UTC precision, 400/401/403/429/503, bounded SQL, HTTP privacy.

9. **P1 PREVIEW1600-09 (A/C):** aggregated admin KPI cohort>=20, edge privacy/SEO, no sensitive logs, 320px WCAG 2.2 AA.

## v2026.11.01.1598 — F675-205 Consent-Fenced Daily Digest and Durable Dedupe (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle and source:** Previous Feature Addition v1596 → Current Feature Improvement v1598 → Next Feature Addition v1600 (provisional). At start and midpoint, origin/main = f13bbce273ffc65e8576170992d82ea00c27a1c9. Authority: main AGENTS.md, README.md, English PROJECT_PLAN.md (canonical), Korean parity; previous planning Draft #2297 remains unmerged. Development issue #2296 and Draft PR #2301. This is a documentation-only correction to proposed F675-205, not a shipped feature. No new distributed feature-plan file.

### Four defects corrected before implementation

**D1 — Consent withdrawal and opt-out cannot be guaranteed by a preference-row lock alone (P0).** The v1596 worker locks only the digest preference and rechecks consent. A concurrent consent withdrawal through another transaction can commit between the check and inbox insert; the old text's “disable/revoke before commit prevents new digest” claim was not proven. **Chosen:** a shared, reviewed per-member authorization serialization protocol across worker, digest-toggle and existing consent-revocation/account-deletion paths, with a monotonic consent generation or equivalent durable revocation fence. Lock ordering must be identical in every path (member authorization row → preference → receipt → inbox), and worker must validate generation and enabled status under that lock immediately before the atomic insert. An already committed notification remains historical; a revocation serialized before worker authorization must prevent a new one. If the existing revocation path cannot participate, do not claim this guarantee or enable the worker: **P0 BLOCKED**. A caller-writable session setting is not identity proof. A consent grant after withdrawal must NOT silently restore a previously enabled digest: persist OFF until a fresh authenticated opt-in. Require race tests with explicit commit-order assertions, not merely simultaneous requests.

**D2 — SENT receipts must survive inbox retention without blocking deletion (P0).** v1596 proposed a receipt.notification_id and an outcome/notification-id consistency CHECK, but did not specify the notification table's authoritative PK/FK or deletion policy. A strong FK plus SENT-requires-ID CHECK and ON DELETE SET NULL can make normal inbox retention fail. **Chosen:** immutable unique (user_id, digest_date) receipt as the dedupe authority, independent of the current inbox row's lifetime; a SENT receipt records the committed insertion result, not current inbox existence or user read status. Do not introduce an FK/ON DELETE behavior until clean-schema DDL and retention/deletion are reviewed; choose either a retention-compatible nullable reference with separate historical state or an explicitly non-FK opaque insertion identifier, after security review. A SKIPPED_ZERO receipt is terminal for that KST date: new holdings at 10:00 do not generate a second digest. Deleting an inbox row must not permit replay. Account deletion must remove/anonymize preference/receipt according to reviewed policy, without retaining member UUID indefinitely. **P0 BLOCKED** until clean-install PostgreSQL proves actual in_app_notifications DDL (only test fixtures were found in numbered-migration search).

**D3 — Wall-clock deadline and transaction time have different semantics.** v1596 promises 09:00–11:00 KST but uses a statement_timestamp as the count basis. A transaction that starts before 11:00 can commit after 11:00; a precommit clock check cannot mathematically guarantee commit before a deadline. **Chosen:** only claim work when database clock is in [09:00,11:00) Asia/Seoul, use a single statement_timestamp for both disjoint expiry bands, derive digest_date from that database instant, recheck database clock and feature flag before the write, and abort when cutoff already observed. Do not begin new claims at/after 11:00, never backfill another KST day. An already in-flight commit may complete marginally after 11:00; user copy says “scheduled around 09:00, retries normally stop at 11:00; delivery not guaranteed,” not a strict commit-time SLA. Reconcile worker/server clock skew and prove KST date rollover in PostgreSQL; do not derive date from application-local time or transaction_timestamp held across batches. Add bounded worker cancellation and a per-owner transaction timeout; do not kill shared processes.

**D4 — Scheduler eligibility and notification link are not established by existing code.** Current Nest NotificationService directly reads public.in_app_notifications and its safeNotificationLink allowlist omits /inventory. Notification DTO has PRODUCT_ACTIVITY, but this is not proof that a fresh database can create/store a digest or that app-role grants are least privilege. **Chosen:** schema provenance/ownership/constraints/retention first, then an explicit exact-path /inventory allowlist addition with malicious URL and Android deep-link negative tests. Scheduler principal gets only reviewed function EXECUTE and bounded member eligibility, not arbitrary user_items or finance DML. Preserve the default-OFF feature switch and reject all error-as-empty behavior. A worker must not claim SENT if inbox insert fails. Do not reuse an unrelated notification category as authorization.

### Revised member/API/DB contract and verification gates

- **User value, audience, entry, CTA, states:** unchanged opt-in owner-only /account/notifications switch, companion /inventory settings link, 09:00 KST in-app digest with 0–24h and 24–72h distinct-item counts, no names/amounts/IDs; Enable, Disable, Retry, Open inventory. Verified ON/OFF, LOADING, SAVING, VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE, REVISION_CONFLICT, AUTH_REQUIRED, CONSENT_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, OFFLINE and SESSION_CHANGED remain distinct. Disabling after SENT cannot retract an already committed inbox entry. A SKIPPED_ZERO day must not be shown as a missed-delivery error.
- **API:** GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preferences and CSRF-guarded PUT with expectedRevision decimal string and server-derived actor; 200 VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE only for matching revision, 409 stale, 401/403/429/503 fail closed, GET reconciliation after ambiguous write. Add a server-authored consentGeneration/eligibilityRevision only if supported by the reviewed authorization boundary; never trust client-supplied generation. The preference stays OFF on consent withdrawal and cannot be reenabled by a stale PUT.
- **SQL/transaction:** forward-only schema number only after migration-318 collision; owner preference and (user_id,KST date) unique receipt; worker authorization serialization shared with revocation, preference row lock, receipt uniqueness, one verified inventory aggregate, inbox insertion and SENT receipt in the same transaction. SKIPPED_ZERO receipt on verified zero only. Crash before COMMIT ⇒ neither inbox nor receipt; crash after COMMIT ⇒ retry sees receipt and does not duplicate. Retention deletion cannot erase dedupe prematurely. No ledger, WLD, item or reward mutation.
- **Admin/security/SEO/mobile/a11y/KPI:** aggregated cohorts ≥20 only, no owner IDs or notification bodies in telemetry; success/error private/no-store/noindex/nosniff/referrer headers at Nest, Next, app-api, Android gateway and edge. 320px, 200% zoom, 44px controls, WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard/aria-live and KO/EN parity. Android account-switch fences all pending responses and uses only validated /inventory deep link. Targets: zero post-revocation newly authorized digests, zero duplicate SENT per KST date, zero finance/item deltas; p95 and job completion require measured Test evidence, not estimates.
- **QA acceptance (NOT RUN):** isolated PostgreSQL 17 clean + upgrade, two owners and direct app-role actor-spoof negative, withdrawal vs claim in both commit orders, stale opt-in after reconsent, account deletion, simultaneous workers, SKIPPED_ZERO then new holdings, SENT inbox deletion and replay, rollback/crash on either side of commit, 08:59:59/09:00/10:59:59/11:00 KST, midnight rollover, 1µs 24/72h boundaries, 10,001 holdings, 429/503/409, forged links, edge headers on errors, Android logout and accessibility. Test scheduler fairness/100-row batch throughput and cgroup headroom before claiming daily delivery.
- **P0/P1 handoff (4 P0 + 6 P1):** P0-01 OPS attest running frontend/backend/edge SHA, independent restore and cgroup capacity (#2171). ## v2026.11.01.1596 — F675-205 Opt-in Owner Inventory Expiry Daily Inbox Digest (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle and authority:** Previous **Feature Improvement v1594** → Current **Feature Addition v1596** → Next **Feature Improvement v1598 (provisional)**. Canonical `origin/main=f13bbce273ffc65e8576170992d82ea00c27a1c9` fetched and rechecked at start and midpoint; `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, English `PROJECT_PLAN.md` and Korean parity are authority. Developer handoff issue **#2296** and planning Draft PR **#2297** are open. Prior planning Draft **#2290** is open/unmerged, so valid F675-199–204 proposals were carried into an isolated documentation branch, not deployed. The feature below is **a proposed design, not implemented**. No new distributed feature-plan file.

### Source-grounded opportunity and alternatives
- `frontend/src/app/inventory/page.tsx` currently uses `apiOrNull('/api/v1/shop/holdings')` and falls back to `[]` on source failure, so empty must never be inferred from that client path. Migration **071** defines `public.user_items(user_id,catalog_id,quantity,expires_at)` with owner/catalog PK; migration **123** exposes `shop_my_items_v2(p_actor)`, excluding expired rows and not independently proving the passed actor is the authenticated owner. Expiry of held inventory is **not** `item_effect_receipts.expires_at`, unpaid upkeep, or financial settlement. F675-203/204 expiry summary/drilldown remain unimplemented Draft designs.
- The Nest `NotificationController` already offers guarded inbox read/read-all with `SessionGuard`, `AuthenticatedGuard`, `ConsentGuard`, and CSRF for writes. `NOTIFICATION_CATEGORIES` includes `PRODUCT_ACTIVITY`; Next `/account/notifications` renders an inbox. However, `safeNotificationLink` currently **does not allow `/inventory`**, and an authoritative `CREATE TABLE public.in_app_notifications` was **not found in inspected numbered migrations** (fixtures are not deployable schema). Treat actual clean-schema presence, constraints, owner privileges and notification indexes as **P0 UNKNOWN/BLOCKED**, not evidence that production is safe.
- Alternative A: browser-only timed toast, rejected because a closed browser never sees it and session state cannot be trusted. Alternative B: external push/email, rejected due to consent, deliverability and PII risk. **Chosen C: opt-in, server-generated, once-per-KST-day in-app digest**, reusing the existing inbox only after clean-schema and permission proof. No push, SMS, email, Discord, financial action or auto-renewal. Independent of unimplemented F675-199–204.

### Member contract, screens, states and timing
- **Purpose/target:** help an authenticated, consent-current inventory owner notice approaching held-item expiry without opening inventory daily. Entry **/account/notifications → Inventory expiry digest** (switch and explanatory text); companion **/inventory → Expiry alerts settings** link. The toggle is **OFF by default**, separate from existing `engagement.notifications_enabled` and security-critical notifications. CTA **Enable daily digest**, **Disable**, **Retry**, **Open inventory**; show last verified settings revision and `Daily around 09:00 Korea time; not guaranteed delivery`. No promise of real-time warnings.
- Server schedule **09:00 Asia/Seoul** daily; process the current KST date only, retry safely until **11:00 KST**, never backfill missed days or send after 11:00. At one PostgreSQL statement timestamp `asOf`, two disjoint future bands are **(asOf,asOf+24h]** and **(asOf+24h,asOf+72h]**, with exact microsecond boundaries. Include only `quantity>0`, `expires_at IS NOT NULL`, and verified owner rows. No effects, upkeep or already expired items. Digest contains **distinct catalog-item counts** in each band (not quantities), no names, amounts, balances or IDs: e.g. `Inventory expiry: 2 kinds within 24h, 3 kinds in the following 48h. Check current inventory; counts may have changed.` Do not send when both counts are zero.
- At most **one committed inbox digest per opted-in owner/KST date**, not guaranteed delivery, and not an authoritative current count. No repeated same-day alert if holdings later change. Notification category `PRODUCT_ACTIVITY`, server-validated link `/inventory` only after allowlist/Android route parity tests; never construct arbitrary URL from notification data. Read/mark-read uses existing guarded inbox paths, not a new admin impersonation endpoint.
- UI states: `FLAG_OFF`, `PREFERENCE_LOADING`, `PREFERENCE_VERIFIED_OFF`, `PREFERENCE_VERIFIED_ON`, `SAVING`, `VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE`, `REVISION_CONFLICT`, `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `CONSENT_REQUIRED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `OFFLINE`, `SESSION_CHANGED`. Failed GET must not render a verified OFF preference; failed PUT must not optimistically claim saved. On 409 refresh setting and request explicit retry. Never claim a scheduled digest was sent merely because the preference is enabled.

### API, database, concurrency, authorization and abuse
- Nest **GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-digest/preferences** returns `{enabled:boolean,revision:string,updatedAtUtc:string|null,sourceStatus:'VERIFIED'}`; **PUT** with CSRF and body `{enabled:boolean,expectedRevision:string}` returns verified new revision or `200 VERIFIED_NO_CHANGE` only if revision matches and desired state is already current. `expectedRevision` is a canonical nonnegative decimal string, not an unsafe JS number. Server derives actor exclusively from authenticated session; no actor UUID in request. 400 malformed, 401 no session, 403 consent/actor mismatch, 409 stale CAS, 429 rate, 503 DB/schema unavailable. No PATCH that silently overwrites another device's choice. No idempotency-key table for this reversible CAS toggle: on ambiguous network completion, GET and reconcile before any new PUT. Rate cap **10 preference writes/member/minute**; backend and Next BFF and Android gateway enforce same contracts.
- Proposed **forward-only**, migration-number-unreserved tables: `inventory_expiry_digest_preferences(user_id uuid PK REFERENCES users(id), enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, revision bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(revision>=0), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL)`; `inventory_expiry_digest_receipts(user_id uuid REFERENCES users(id), digest_date date NOT NULL, outcome text CHECK IN ('SENT','SKIPPED_ZERO'), notification_id uuid NULL, as_of_utc timestamptz NOT NULL, count_24h bigint NOT NULL, count_24_72h bigint NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(user_id,digest_date), CHECK outcome/notification_id consistency)`. Verify actual `in_app_notifications` PK, dedupe_key constraints, foreign keys and migration ownership **before** selecting DDL; do not retrofit applied migration 318 or presume a fixture table is canonical. Suggested indexes: partial `preferences(user_id) WHERE enabled` and existing owner/expiry access path subject to `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on 10,001 rows. No new WLD, item, or ledger writes.
- Preference PUT transaction: session-verified actor → strict CSRF/consent → lock own preference row (insert default row with conflict handling if absent) → compare `expectedRevision` → no-op or increment revision exactly once → commit. All owner checks must be verified against effective app role. **P0 SEC BLOCK:** no new SECURITY DEFINER EXECUTE or direct `user_items`/notification-table grants until two-owner direct-app-role spoof-negative tests and security-owner approval; a caller-controlled `SET LOCAL actor` is not independent authentication. Fixed `search_path=pg_catalog,pg_temp`, schema-qualified objects, migrator-owned functions, PUBLIC revoke. A dedicated restricted scheduler principal must not be the broad web app role.
- Worker: scheduler uses a dedicated reviewed principal to read at most **100 opted-in candidate owner IDs/batch** using a current-date receipt anti-join; then in **one separate DB transaction per owner**, lock that owner preference row with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and recheck enabled/consent, establish one `statement_timestamp()` and KST date, aggregate both bands, then atomically insert **either** `SKIPPED_ZERO` receipt **or** one `PRODUCT_ACTIVITY` inbox row plus `SENT` receipt. Unique `(user_id,digest_date)` is the authoritative dedupe guard across retries, crashes and two workers. Roll back both on any failure; no partial success or fallback fabricated notification. Check feature flag before claim and immediately before commit. Limit statement 2s, lock 500ms, batches 100, and stop at 11:00. These are proposed bounds, not measured throughput. A row committed to inbox is not proof a user read it.
- Scheduler must not have arbitrary finance-table privileges. Disable setting or revoke consent **before commit** prevents new digest; if the transaction already committed, existing inbox message is historical and not remotely unsent. Privacy retention and deletion follow reviewed existing inbox policy; do not invent a retention period. Do not send external channels or enqueue unbounded background work.

### Admin, security, SEO, Android, accessibility, analytics and release
- Admin may see only aggregate operational health: eligible opted-in cohort, attempted owners, SENT/SKIPPED_ZERO, dedupe conflicts, DB failures, lag and p95; suppress any cohort with **<20 distinct members**. No per-user dashboard, raw owner UUID, item names, expiry timestamps, SQL values, notification bodies or links in logs/traces/analytics. Never log preference request body or session token. 0 cross-owner rows and 0 WLD/item/ledger deltas are mandatory targets.
- Every Nest/Next/app-api/Android gateway **success and error** must send `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; exclude settings/inbox from sitemap and search. Verify final HTTP edge headers (#2012), not metadata alone. No third-party tracking or outbound notification. Prevent forged notification links, oversized payloads, mass enumeration and worker replay.
- Next settings panel must fit **320px**, **200% zoom**, **44px** touch targets, keyboard/screen-reader toggle labels, `aria-live` save/conflict feedback without focus theft, reduced motion, KO/EN meaning parity, WCAG **2.2 AA**. Android uses existing authenticated app-api gateway and equivalent toggle, no disk caching, cancel/ignore in-flight replies on logout/account switch using session generation, and map only the validated `/inventory` deep link to the owned-inventory screen.
- KPI acceptance **targets, not measurements**: preference save p95 <300ms; digest job finish by 11:00 KST for eligible cohort under proven capacity; exactly ≤1 committed digest per owner/day, 0 unauthorized reads, 0 ledger/item mutations, and no privacy headers missing. Do not call delivery reliable until repeated full-day simulation proves capacity.
- QA **proposed, NOT RUN**: isolated PostgreSQL 17 clean+upgrade schema and 318 collision; two owner + direct app-role spoof, 10,001 holdings, NULL/expired/zero quantity, 1µs band edges, KST day rollover, DST-independent +09:00, 100 simultaneous worker claims, duplicate retries after commit-lost-response, opt-out/consent race, zero-result receipt, 11:00 cutoff, scheduler restart, 429/503/409, preference CAS on two devices, CSRF, malicious link, cache/noindex on all HTTP statuses, Android account switching, 320px/a11y, 0 finance/item delta. Independent QA must verify clean-schema `in_app_notifications` DDL and constraints before enabling.
- **Release:** flag `inventory_expiry_daily_digest` **OFF** by default; first repair schema parity, app-role privileges, QA v1433 frontend fixture expiry (#2292; 2,899 PASS/2 FAIL on main), Test backend/migrator DB mismatch (#2260), Production locale 500 (#2262), Production extra 9 tables (#2242), 5 checksums and migration-318 conflict (#2233). Separate B SQL/worker, A web, C Android and QA branches; exact candidate SHA Test with real backend+DB+mobile/auth E2E, full CI/security, independent restore and operator-approved GitOps promotion only. Rollback **flag OFF and scheduler stopped first**, then immutable image if needed; retain immutable migration/receipts for audit. **Production RELEASE HOLD**.

## v2026.11.01.1594 — F675-204 Snapshot Equivalence, Canonical Fingerprints and Bounded Pagination (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle / authority:** Previous **Feature Addition v1592** → Current **Feature Improvement v1594** → Next **Feature Addition v1596 (provisional)**. At start and midpoint, `origin/main=f13bbce273ffc65e8576170992d82ea00c27a1c9`; read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, this English canonical plan, Korean parity, SQL migrations 071/123, Nest shop controller/repository, Next `/inventory`, open planning Draft **#2283** and QA **#2285**. Prior planning #2283 is **OPEN/UNMERGED**; valid F675-199–204 proposals are carried into this isolated documentation branch, **not main or runtime**. Handoff **#2282**. **DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD; no implementation.**

### Four source-grounded design corrections and chosen trade-offs

1. **D1 — an unchanged fingerprint cannot prove that no mutation occurred (ABA).** The v1592 contract promises HTTP 409 for *any* insertion/deletion/update between pages. An item may be removed and reinserted, or its quantity changed and restored, leaving the same full-band digest. A stateless read-only fingerprint detects **different observable state at verification time**, not historical mutation events. **Chosen A:** document state-equivalence, with 409 only when the current complete ordered source differs from the initial source. An ABA returning to identical state is **not** guaranteed to return 409; never describe the result as a transactionally frozen snapshot or a mutation audit. **Rejected B:** a persistent per-owner mutation revision would detect ABA but requires updating every item/catalog write path, migration and write audit, violating this independent read-only feature's bounded scope. If the product later requires event-history detection, a separate reviewed revision design is a prerequisite, not a hidden promise. The UI labels results “Verified against the saved view as of [KST]” and “May change; refresh to view current holdings.”
2. **D2 — a digest without a canonical byte contract is unverifiable.** Build one ordered source sequence using `(expires_at,catalog_id)` and **exactly** `[catalog_id UUID text, expires_at UTC six-microsecond string, quantity canonical decimal string, catalog code, catalog name, category]` per owner-scoped row. PostgreSQL 17 proposed digest: `encode(sha256(convert_to(coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_array(...) ORDER BY expires_at,catalog_id),'[]'::jsonb)::text,'UTF8')),'hex')`; ensure `jsonb_agg` is ordered *inside* the aggregate and `asOf` is the original token value. Include a versioned algorithm ID and original band in the AEAD token; never hash JS `Date`, unordered `json_agg`, locale-formatted labels, effect-expiry or unverified client data. First page, fingerprint, keyset and `hasMore` must come from **one READ COMMITTED SQL statement**. Each next page recomputes and compares the same full-band digest **before** returning rows; a different digest ⇒ `409 SNAPSHOT_CHANGED`, including display metadata changes. A hash match is state equivalence, **not proof against SHA-256 collision or ABA**. Validate PG17 `sha256` availability and exact byte fixtures before grant.
3. **D3 — a fixed 120-second cursor cannot reasonably traverse 10,001 holdings at 20/page and 30 requests/min.** Keep **20/page default, 50/page maximum**, and **30 member requests/minute** shared by initial/page calls, but renew a sealed cursor after **each successful nonfinal page** for up to **120 seconds of inactivity**, while enforcing an immutable **30-minute absolute session ceiling** from the first query. The AEAD payload binds member, authenticated session generation, band, immutable original `asOf`, algorithm version, initial digest, stable `(expires_at,catalog_id)` keyset, initial maximum page limit, `firstIssuedAt`, `issuedAt`, and `expiresAt=min(now+120s,firstIssuedAt+1800s)`; all times server-generated. The original `asOf` and digest **never refresh** on renewal. At expiry return `410 SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED`, at changed data `409 SNAPSHOT_CHANGED`, and provide **Restart results**; do not silently combine old and new pages. At 10,001 holdings, 20/page needs up to 501 requests (≥16.7 minutes at 30/min) and therefore remains a **best-effort browsing path**, not a promise of uninterrupted completion. After 60 seconds display a prominent snapshot-as-of/stale label; no live-availability claim.
4. **D4 — unbounded full-band hashing can exhaust memory and produce partial truth.** Proposed guardrails: maximum **20,000 matching rows/band**, maximum **4 MiB UTF-8 canonical aggregate**, and **2-second read statement timeout**, all to be validated by `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and isolated PG17 tests before activation. Before constructing JSONB, preflight the complete ordered source in the same statement with a 20,001-row sentinel and exact canonical encoded-byte budget; never allocate an unbounded aggregate and only then discover an overrun. If a bound is exceeded, digest cannot be computed, an owner join is invalid, or a DB/clock error occurs, return sanitized `503 SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` / `SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, **never** `200 VERIFIED_EMPTY`, truncated `hasMore=false`, or an unchecked page. If a client loses connectivity, discard unverified appended rows. 20,001-row and 4 MiB overrun fixtures must demonstrate fail-closed behavior. No index or migration number is reserved while migration-318 conflict #2233 remains unresolved.

### Complete revised feature contract (proposal only)

- **Purpose / audience / permission / entry:** signed-in, consent-current owner only; existing `/inventory` → **Expiring soon** → choose **0–24h**, **24–72h**, or **72–168h** → **Show items**, **Load more**, **Restart results**, and existing inventory-row CTA. Band wire values `24h`,`72h`,`168h` mean *those three disjoint bands*, **not** cumulative 0–72h/0–168h. The original PostgreSQL `statement_timestamp()` defines `(asOf,asOf+24h]`, `(asOf+24h,asOf+72h]`, `(asOf+72h,asOf+168h]`, with exact UTC microseconds. Exclude NULL/expired/zero-quantity, effect-expiry and upkeep; never mutate items, ledger or WLD. Flag `inventory_expiry_drilldown` **OFF** by default and independent of unimplemented F675-199–203.
- **API / states:** authenticated guarded `GET /api/v1/shop/expiry-urgency/items?band=24h|72h|168h&limit=20` and CSRF-protected `POST /api/v1/shop/expiry-urgency/items/pages` with `{pageToken,limit}`; server-derived actor only, 1..50 integer limit, page limit no higher than initial ceiling. `200` only for verified nonempty/empty, canonical six-digit UTC timestamps and decimal quantity strings, `hasMore`, optional renewed `pageToken`, `snapshotAsOf`, `snapshotExpiresAt`; `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden/invalid token, `409` changed source, `410` expired token, `429` rate limit, `503` source unavailable/limit. UI states LOADING, VERIFIED_ITEMS, VERIFIED_EMPTY, SNAPSHOT_STALE, RESTART_REQUIRED, UNAVAILABLE, OFFLINE, FLAG_OFF, SESSION_CHANGED. Reject duplicate/out-of-order cursor rows and malformed JSON/number/time, never render an error as an empty inventory.
- **DB / transaction / authorization:** one owner-scoped read-only SQL statement per request with a stable original `asOf`, exact UTC six-digit serialization in SQL, deterministic ordering, count/digest/cursor within that statement; no cross-request DB transaction, no persistent snapshot or audit revision. Migration 071 owner/catalog PK, migration 123 `shop_my_items_v2(p_actor)` with supplied actor and no DB-authenticated actor proof. **P0 SECURITY BLOCK:** do not grant new SECURITY DEFINER EXECUTE to `moneyverse_app` until independently reviewed actor binding or privilege-isolated read gateway, direct-app-role two-owner spoof negative tests, and explicit security owner approval. Keep table grants revoked, `SET search_path=pg_catalog,pg_temp`, migrator function ownership, PUBLIC revoke; verify query plan before optional owner/expiry index. Never use caller-writable `SET LOCAL actor` as attestation.
- **Admin / privacy / SEO / mobile / a11y / KPI:** no admin impersonation, only aggregated cohort≥20 page-load, 409/410/429/503 and p95 metrics; no actor, token, item, expiry, cursor or fingerprint in logs. All Nest/Next/Android gateway/edge **success and errors**: `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; exclude private pages from sitemap. 320px, 200% zoom, 44px targets, keyboard/focus/aria-live, reduced motion, KO/EN parity; discard late responses and in-memory rows on logout/account switch. p95<250ms at 10,001 rows and zero cross-owner reads/shared-cache responses are **targets, not measurements**.
- **QA / deployment / rollback:** disposable PG17 clean+upgrade, two owners including direct-app-role arbitrary-actor attempts, 10,001 and 20,001 holdings, >4MiB metadata, canonical Unicode/delimiter/NULL metadata, SHA-256 deterministic byte fixture, ±1µs band edges, source change vs ABA restored-state, repeated cursor renewals and 120s inactivity/30min absolute expiry, 30/min throttling, 401/403/409/410/429/503, CSRF, malformed/tampered/cross-session token, Android/web/edge privacy, zero ledger/item delta, flag OFF, rollback. Developer B owns approved SQL/API; A web; C Android; QA independent. Separate exact-SHA Test with verified backend/migrator DB parity and independent restore, then explicit operator Production approval; **never deploy from planning**. Roll back flag first, then immutable image, leave forward-only migration intact.

### Prioritized development handoff — 4 P0 + 6 P1 (all OPEN)
