### Purpose, alternatives, dependencies and member journey
- **Purpose and target:** consent-current authenticated inventory owners want to place a limited **one-time forecast** of their own expiring holdings into a personal calendar without manually retyping dates. Existing `/inventory` only lists holdings; F675-199 `/inventory/expiry-calendar` is an unimplemented, flagged-OFF prerequisite. This feature must not be described as available until both are built, accepted and released. Export is NOT a subscription, live sync, notification receipt, reservation, money transfer or guarantee that an item will still be held on the date.
- **Options:** A) browser-only `.ics` from existing unbounded holdings (reject: `apiOrNull` can false-empty, inconsistent per-row expiry clocks, 10,001+ payload, leak to client); B) calendar OAuth/webcal subscription (reject: third-party credentials, public/tokenized URLs, sync and retention burden); C) **chosen:** authenticated, explicit one-time server-generated `.ics` of aggregate **KST dates only**, using the proposed F675-199 owner-scoped one-statement read. No permanent export table, third-party API, calendar permissions, background jobs or finance writes.
- **Entry:** `/inventory` → `/inventory/expiry-calendar` → “Download calendar (.ics)” → confirmation dialog with 7/30-day selector and warning “This file may be stored by your calendar app; deleting an item in Moneyverse will not remove imported events.” Explicit “Download once” / “Cancel” CTA; no automatic download, URL subscription, auto-import, background share or default opt-in. Show DB-derived as-of KST time and count of exported dates after a verified result; disclose that reopening/importing again may leave old events or create duplicates depending on calendar app. Do not promise deduplication or deletion.
- **States:** IDLE, CONFIRMATION, GENERATING, VERIFIED_FILE_READY(200), VERIFIED_EMPTY(204; no file), INVALID_REQUEST(400), AUTH_REQUIRED(401), CONSENT_REQUIRED(403), ACCOUNT_CHANGED(409; discard bytes), RATE_LIMITED(429; Retry-After), SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE(503; no file), OFFLINE, CANCELLED. On source/ACL/timeout error never generate a zero-event success file, never treat null as empty, never reuse a prior member's blob. Date/amount data are **expiry forecasts**, not delivered reminders.

### Exact request, response, privacy and calendar format contract
- **Nest internal API:** `POST /api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/export` JSON `{windowDays:7|30}`, exactly one allowlisted key; 2KiB max request, no caller-provided owner/asOf/timezone/filename/UID or item IDs. SessionGuard + AuthenticatedGuard + ConsentGuard and same-origin CSRF at Next; backend actor is derived from verified session. Next same-origin BFF `POST /api/inventory/expiry-calendar/export` via `server-only` API client; Android authenticated `/app-api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/export` parity through existing gateway. Do not publish Nest as an open edge prefix. Proposed owner rate cap 3/minute and 10/day, IP resource ceiling and one concurrent export per actor; tune from measurements, not claimed production thresholds.
- **Response:** `200 Content-Type: text/calendar; charset=utf-8` with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="moneyverse-expiry-YYYYMMDD.ics"` where YYYYMMDD is server KST date; ≤64KiB total, ≤30 `VEVENT` (one per nonempty KST date, not per item). `204` only after a successful owner DB query proves no eligible dates; `400/401/403/409/429/503` must carry no calendar bytes, with bounded sanitized error and `Retry-After` for 429. Set `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Vary: Cookie` as appropriate on 200/204/errors at Next/Nest/Android/real edge. No GET, public link, sitemap, search indexing or cache key reuse. Use a fixed server filename (not user-controlled), no reflection in file content or headers.
- **RFC 5545:** UTF-8, CRLF on every content line; fold at ≤75 **octets**, never split a UTF-8 code point, use CRLF + SPACE continuation; escape TEXT backslash, comma, semicolon and newline and reject NUL/control/CRLF injection. `BEGIN:VCALENDAR`, `VERSION:2.0`, fixed `PRODID`, `CALSCALE:GREGORIAN`, `METHOD:PUBLISH`; one `VEVENT` per verified nonempty date with `UID`, `DTSTAMP` (DB as-of UTC rounded to seconds for RFC syntax), `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD` of the **next KST date** (exclusive), `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT`, fixed Korean `SUMMARY` with exact decimal type count, and `DESCRIPTION` with exact unit count plus snapshot/no-sync warning. All-day DATE avoids UTC-to-device date drift; no `TZID` for DATE values. No item name, actor UUID, email, external URL, `ATTENDEE`, `GEO`, `VALARM`, financial data or opaque signed token in the file.
- **Stable UID privacy:** `UID` is an HMAC-SHA256-derived opaque, domain-separated identifier over actor UUID + KST date + format version, rendered as a bounded lowercase hex string at a fixed non-routable `@moneyverse.invalid` suffix; server secret never exposed. Identical actor/day/version can yield stable UID on re-export, but import clients MAY still duplicate or preserve deleted events. Do not assert guaranteed updates; rotation policy must retain old-key UID derivation for compatibility or explicitly version/break and warn. Constant-time token checks apply where tokens exist; UID is not an authentication credential.

### DB snapshot, invariants, transaction and operational boundaries
- **Read source:** one primary PostgreSQL statement captures `asOfUtc` once and `kstToday` in `Asia/Seoul`, then filters `user_items` for authenticated owner, `quantity>0`, non-null `expires_at>asOfUtc` and expiry in [KST today 00:00, today+7/30 days 00:00). Count **catalog types** as owner+catalog PK rows and **units** with `SUM(quantity)::bigint` serialized as exact decimal strings, never JS Number for large values. Group by local expiry date, sort ascending, at most 30 groups. Calendar event date is expiry's KST calendar day, not effect expiry, billing, notification delivery or future holding proof. Empty is verified only after the SQL succeeds.
- **Privileges/constraints:** reuse the proposed F675-199 owner summary read model; if absent, implement a coordinated forward-only migrator-owned `SECURITY DEFINER` read function with fixed `search_path`, explicit owner filter, qualified relations, `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC` and only `GRANT EXECUTE` to app role. Do not grant direct SELECT/DML on `user_items` or any finance table; current DEV app ACL discrepancy #993 blocks release. Existing PK(user_id,catalog_id), quantity constraint and expiry semantics remain authoritative. No new persistent table, index or write transaction by default. A partial index `(user_id,expires_at,catalog_id) WHERE quantity>0 AND expires_at IS NOT NULL` is a **candidate only** after EXPLAIN/BUFFERS at 10,001+ rows and write-cost review; coordinate migration numbering with Backend B.
- **Consistency:** a single DB statement supplies one MVCC snapshot; `asOfUtc` is the reference for all rows. The downloaded file is a snapshot, not a cross-request transaction, a live sync or an immutable history. If F675-199's calendar summary is called separately for UI preview, the export may differ; present the export's own as-of and counts. No client-supplied digest can authorize another owner's export. Abort on account/consent/session epoch change before response commit; on streaming error discard the file, never return a partial 200. Generate bounded bytes fully before setting 200 headers; 64KiB limit overflow/invalid source → 503 with no partial ICS. No changes to holdings, receipts, account_balances, ledger_postings, WLD or database schema during planning.

### Administration, abuse, mobile, SEO, analytics, tests and rollout
- **Security/abuse:** authenticated owner BOLA and consent-negative tests, CSRF and replay protection for POST (read-only export; no financial idempotency receipt), resource/rate limiting, secret rotation, no untrusted calendar TEXT or filenames, fixed content headers and no user-data logging. Logs contain only anonymous error class, duration, event count and safe release version. Rate-limited and source-unverified errors are distinct. Recheck privacy headers on real edge, not only Next metadata. External calendar apps receive data **only through an explicit user action**, beyond Moneyverse's revocation boundary.
- **Web/Android/a11y:** 320px, 200% zoom, WCAG 2.2 AA, 44px controls, visible confirmation, keyboard Escape/Cancel and focus return, screen-reader aria-live states without focus theft, reduced motion. Android must use explicit OS share/download intent with ephemeral scoped URI and revoke it on completion, never background upload, persistent private cache, auto-open another app, or keep bytes after logout/account switch. Browser must revoke object URLs and clear bytes on navigation/account change; no public SEO, sitemap or indexable member export URL.
- **Admin/KPI:** admin sees only weekly aggregated export starts, verified 200/204, 400/409/429/503, 7/30 selection, import warning acknowledgement, p50/p95 SQL+serialization latency, size cap rejects and account-switch drops; suppress cohorts <20 distinct members, no item names, actor IDs, UID or file contents. Proposed targets: 0 cross-owner files, 0 ledger writes, 0 partial files, 0 ICS parser failures, p95<500ms at 10,001 holdings; **unmeasured acceptance targets**.
- **P0 backlog (4):** OPS1576-01 (#1984/#2144/#2171) prove Production executable/backend/frontend/edge SHA, immutable manifest, cgroup headroom, independent restore/rollback; SEC1576-02 (#993/#828/#2111) reconcile live app grants and checksum parity and cross-owner ACL; FIN1576-03 (#1976/#2191, Draft #2221) prove Treasury and marketplace ledger provenance, no unledgered settlement; REL1576-04 (#1088/#2144, QA Draft #2220) required CI/security, official Test **exact new SHA** authenticated E2E and independent restore before operator-approved GitOps Production promotion. QA #2220's repaired Test verifier validated only the **old deployed Test SHA**, not latest main; Production manifest remains missing. **P0 RELEASE HOLD.**
- **P1 backlog (6):** EXPORT1576-05 Backend B owner SQL one-statement as-of/group/bigint/EXPLAIN; EXPORT1576-06 Backend B RFC5545 encoder/UID/64KiB/fail-closed; EXPORT1576-07 Backend B Nest auth/CSRF/2KiB/rate/status; EXPORT1576-08 Dev A/C Next and Android confirmation, download/share, a11y, account-switch; EXPORT1576-09 Dev A/C edge privacy/SEO, aggregate KPI and flag; EXPORT1576-10 QA isolated PG17 10,001 rows, two owners, two concurrent exports, KST midnight ±1µs, null/expired/zero quantity, 7/30 boundary, 30 events, 64KiB, UTF-8/CRLF injection, forged identity, 204 vs 503, 429, Android/Next/edge, RFC parser roundtrip, no ledger writes and rollback. **ALL PROPOSED, NOT RUN.** Separate A/B/C/QA branches; no edits to their runtime work.
- **Deployment/rollback:** feature `INVENTORY_EXPIRY_CALENDAR_EXPORT_ENABLED` defaults OFF and requires F675-199 source gate. Schema migrations forward-only if needed, staged OFF → internal → limited cohort → monitored wider rollout only after complete CI, security/audit, exact-SHA official Test and independent restore, then explicit operator approval. Roll back by OFF, not destructive migration; already imported third-party calendar files **cannot be remotely revoked**. No Production promotion by planning.
- **External independent evidence:** IETF RFC 5545 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545.html) and OWASP reflective-file-download guidance (https://owasp-aasvs4.readthedocs.io/en/latest/12.3.4.html) consulted as specification sources; not counted as accepted corpus records. Newly evidence-approved/deduplicated/classified **0**; cumulative **UNKNOWN / 10,000**; gate **BLOCKED / IN PROGRESS**. Documentation-only design; no acceptance, runtime, DB, WLD, ledger, Test or Production change.


## v2026.10.31.1574 — F675-199 Expiry Calendar Cross-Request Consistency Hardening (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Cycle and source:** Previous Feature Addition v1572 → Current Feature Improvement v1574 → Next Feature Addition v1576 (provisional). Canonical main 353c6d5d6ddbc14b1067e84f9c4a127bab1c3834 checked at start and midpoint. The predecessor Draft PR #2212 was CLOSED WITHOUT MERGE at 22:49 KST, and its branch was deleted; this branch starts from the current main and explicitly recovers the valuable F675-199 design below. Current main still labels planning v1518, so do not imply that intervening proposals were merged. Draft PR #2218 OPEN/DRAFT/HOLD; GitHub handoff issue #2211 remains OPEN (comment 6544459745). This is documentation only, not a running calendar or a deployment.

### Defect and decision
- **Source-backed defect in the proposed contract, not a production incident:** v1572 returns asOfUtc from summary and day reads, but the day request schema carries only kstDate/limit/cursor. It does not bind first-page/day continuation to the summary's database as-of instant. Existing shop_my_items_v2 (migration 123) calls clock_timestamp() in its expiry filter and cannot provide a pinned cross-request inventory view. If an item expires, a catalog label changes, or KST midnight passes between summary and detail, independently evaluated pages may disagree while appearing to be one coherent calendar. The proposed day fingerprint alone does not establish that the first day page matches the summary.
- **Alternatives:** A) reuse existing holdings + browser filtering (reject: false-empty on apiOrNull failure, per-row clock and unbounded payload); B) persistent per-member snapshots (reject for V1: new retention/PII and write-path complexity); C) **chosen** stateless, short-lived, HMAC-bound read context with per-day complete-set digest and fresh DB validation. No new write tables, no reminder dependency, no WLD/ledger mutation. The 120-second lifetime is a proposal requiring load validation, not an observed SLA.

### Exact member/API/DB contract
- **Entry and UX:** /inventory → /inventory/expiry-calendar; owner-only consent-current member, default next 7 KST dates or switch to 30, select a day, paginate 20 (max 50), Refresh, Back. Status states LOADING, VERIFIED_DAYS, VERIFIED_EMPTY, VERIFIED_DAY_EMPTY, MORE_ITEMS, STALE_VIEW (409), AUTH_REQUIRED (401), CONSENT_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (503), ACCOUNT_CHANGED. Never turn an upstream error into zero items. Display "As of [KST timestamp]; this is an expiry forecast, not a reminder receipt"; after 409 discard all displayed day pages, refetch summary and restore focus. Keep 320px/200% zoom, WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard and screen-reader announcements, reduced motion and Android parity.
- **POST summary:** /api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/summary {windowDays:7|30}, auth+consent+CSRF, 2KiB max request, proposed owner 20 reads/min. In ONE primary-DB statement capture one asOfUtc and KST today; evaluate eligible owner user_items rows with quantity>0, non-null expires_at, expires_at>asOfUtc and expires_at in [KST today 00:00, KST today+windowDays 00:00). Return 200 VERIFIED with {asOfUtc,kstToday,windowDays,viewToken,days:[{kstDate,typeCount,unitCount,dayToken,earliestExpiryUtc}],totalTypes,totalUnits}; verified empty only after successful query. dayToken is a backend-HMAC-signed envelope bound to hash(viewToken), KST date and a complete selected-day deterministic digest, including each row's catalog_id, exact microsecond expires_at, quantity and ALL display-relevant catalog fields; canonical ordered/length-delimited encoding avoids concatenation collisions. Count distinct owner+catalog PK rows separately from summed units (bigint decimal strings).
- **View token:** backend signs version, actor UUID, authenticated session/account epoch, asOfUtc with six-digit microsecond precision, kstToday, windowDays, issuedAt, and expiresAt=min(asOfUtc+120 seconds,next KST midnight). Derive actor and account epoch from server session, not client input. Token is opaque HMAC with rotation/key ID, constant-time verification, max 2KiB request including token. On continuation at or after expiresAt or after KST rollover return 409 STALE_VIEW, never 200 verified-empty; no caller-supplied arbitrary asOf.
- **POST day:** /api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/day initial {viewToken,kstDate,dayToken,limit:20|50}; continuation {viewToken,kstDate,dayToken,limit,cursor}. kstDate must be inside signed 7/30-day window. Recompute complete-day digest and keyset result from ONE primary-DB statement using the SIGNED asOfUtc (not a new clock_timestamp in WHERE), and compare to the digest extracted ONLY from the verified signed dayToken; reject an unsigned/client-supplied digest; mismatch → 409 STALE_VIEW. Order by (expires_at ASC,catalog_id ASC) with exact timestamptz microseconds, no JS Date equality and no OFFSET. HMAC cursor binds viewToken digest, signed dayToken digest, owner/session epoch, day, full-day digest, last exact UTC expiry and catalog UUID, version and remaining TTL. Invalid token → 400/403; cross-account → 403; unknown DB/ACL/schema → 503; never silently restart page two. Client must not combine data from different view tokens. A catalog display-name edit or same-count item replacement must invalidate the digest.
- **Consistency boundary:** a single statement gives a consistent MVCC snapshot; separate HTTP requests do NOT share a PostgreSQL transaction snapshot. Digest equality certifies equivalent selected-day content at the two observed statements, not historical absence of an intervening change (ABA) or global consistency across unrelated dates. Items expiring after asOf remain part of the explicitly labeled as-of forecast until refresh or TTL; no claim of current live holdings after asOf. Day detail must not imply summary-wide atomicity. If fingerprint generation cannot be proven correct/fast, keep flag OFF and return 503, not an unsigned cursor.
- **DB privileges:** forward-only SECURITY DEFINER owner-filtered functions owned by migrator, fixed search_path, EXECUTE-only moneyverse_app, no direct table grants. Existing shop_my_items_v2(actor) is not suitable as the pinned asOf source. Nest must derive actor from authenticated session; passing p_actor to SECURITY DEFINER is not itself independent proof of the caller's identity if app DB credentials are compromised. Preserve existing role boundary and document residual risk. Index (user_id,expires_at,catalog_id) partial candidate only after EXPLAIN ANALYZE BUFFERS and write-cost evidence. Do not edit existing migrations.
- **Privacy, admin, SEO and mobile:** private/no-store, noindex, no-referrer on 200/4xx/5xx at Next/Nest/Android, no sitemap, no query-string item IDs or personal analytics, Vary Cookie where appropriate, account-switch fencing. Admin only aggregates >=20 distinct members; track summary/day/7-to-30 adoption, 409, 429, 503, p95 and cursor retries without member item identifiers. p95<300ms is an unmeasured target. Feature INVENTORY_EXPIRY_CALENDAR_ENABLED defaults OFF.

### Engineering handoff and release gates (4 P0 + 6 P1)
- **P0 OPS1574-01** (#1984/#2144/#2171): exact running backend/frontend/edge SHA provenance, cgroup task headroom, independent restore and rollback; do not terminate peer agents.
- **P0 SEC1574-02** (#993/#2111): reconcile PG17 checksums and app ACL; prove no direct user_items or finance DML grants and no cross-member exposure.
- **P0 FIN1574-03** (#1976/#2153/#2191): prove Treasury/marketplace ledger provenance before any release; calendar itself is read-only with zero WLD/ledger writes.
- **P0 REL1574-04** (#1088/#1663/#2206): recover closed-unmerged planning evidence, reconcile competing A/B/C/QA branches, official Test exact-SHA authenticated E2E, independent restore and explicit operator promotion.
- **P1 CAL1574-05 Backend B:** summary one-statement asOf+KST horizon+per-day HMAC-signed digest token; EXPLAIN for 10,001 rows and bigint correctness.
- **P1 CAL1574-06 Backend B:** HMAC viewToken/day cursor, microsecond keyset, day digest recheck, KST rollover/TTL 409 and key rotation.
- **P1 CAL1574-07 Backend B:** Nest auth/consent/CSRF schemas and 200/400/401/403/409/429/503 source-state; 2KiB body and proposed rate cap.
- **P1 CAL1574-08 Dev A/C:** Next/Android parity, verified-empty vs 503, account switch, screen reader/focus/zoom, no false live-claim.
- **P1 CAL1574-09 Dev A/C:** all-edge privacy/SEO headers, flag OFF, aggregate-only admin metrics and measured performance.
- **P1 CAL1574-10 QA:** disposable PG17 10,001 rows, two owners, two concurrent readers, KST midnight ±1µs, same-millisecond different-microsecond expiries, expiry between pages, same-count replacement, catalog rename, 119/120/121-second TTL, cross-account cursor, 64-bit counts, app ACL denial, no ledger writes, Android/Next and rollback regression. **PROPOSED NOT RUN.**
- **Gate:** previous detailed QA v1420 FAILED/P0 (backend 2786 PASS/501 SKIP, frontend 2776 PASS, isolated PG17 312/312, full audit 13 advisories, Test FX500, DB ACL/checksums, finance provenance, exact-SHA Test/restore unresolved). A fresh complete QA pass is NOT evidenced in this planning run. Build Production Release workflow on main was IN_PROGRESS at 23:05 KST; no outcome or release authorization inferred. Implementation requires separate development branches, forward-only migration, Test exact-SHA gate and manual promotion. Roll back by flag OFF, never destructive schema rollback. **DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD.**
- **External independent evidence gate:** newly verified/deduplicated/evidence-classified references 0; cumulative approved count UNKNOWN / 10,000. **BLOCKED / IN PROGRESS**, not complete.

## v2026.10.31.1572 — F675-199 Owner Inventory Expiry Calendar (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)
**Historical status correction:** predecessor Draft #2212 CLOSED UNMERGED at 2026-10-31 22:49 KST; archived proposal retained here as source material, not as merged implementation.

**Cycle/authority:** Previous Feature Improvement v1570 → Current Feature Addition v1572 → Next Feature Improvement v1574 (provisional). Canonical main 5bccda44d6db56aff05fa5623ef7f72b2ec0263c checked at start and midpoint; unmerged planning parent Draft #2203; development handoff issue #2211. This is a proposed design, not implemented or deployed. English canonical, Korean equivalent. F675-192–198 are also unmerged proposals; calendar V1 must not depend on their runtime existence.

### Purpose, alternatives, member flow and states
- **Problem:** the current /inventory view lists owner holdings but does not provide a day-based forecast of when multiple held items expire. A member should be able to plan before expiry without falsely assuming that a reminder has been delivered. This is a read-only inventory aid, not an alert delivery or purchase feature.
- **Options:** (A) filter existing inventory client-side: inexpensive but can mistake an upstream failure for an empty list and is not safe for 10,001 holdings; (B) rely on unimplemented reminder-preview F675-194: couples an inventory view to consent/mute/digest and gives a different eligibility definition; (C) **chosen** owner-scoped DB aggregate and bounded per-day details, independent of reminder opt-in. No email/push, auto-renew, equip, purchase, WLD or ledger changes.
- **Audience/entry:** authenticated consent-current member only. From /inventory → /inventory/expiry-calendar. Default next 7 KST calendar dates; switch to next 30 dates; choose a date to open its detail list. CTA “7 days”, “30 days”, “View items”, “Refresh”, “Back to inventory”. Explain “Expiry forecast is not an alert-delivery record”; nonexpiring holdings remain in ordinary inventory.
- **Truthful states:** LOADING, VERIFIED_DAYS, VERIFIED_EMPTY (only from successful owner DB response), VERIFIED_DAY_EMPTY, MORE_ITEMS, STALE_DAY (409; refresh and restart), AUTH_REQUIRED, CONSENT_REQUIRED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (503), RATE_LIMITED (429), and ACCOUNT_CHANGED (discard stale response). A failed read must never display “no expiring items”. On feature OFF show no navigation or call. Date and count screen-reader announcements, clear focus after filter/detail changes, reduced motion, 44px targets, 320px width/200% zoom, WCAG 2.2 AA; Next and Android parity.
- **Scope:** one user_items row is one catalog **type**; quantity is a separate **unit** count. Include only owner rows with quantity>0, expires_at IS NOT NULL, expires_at>one DB asOf, and expiry in [KST today 00:00, KST today+windowDays 00:00), with 7 or 30 inclusive dates. Midnight exactly at end belongs to the next window and is excluded. A row expiring at 00:00 KST belongs to that date. Group by Asia/Seoul calendar date, not browser timezone; PostgreSQL timestamptz microseconds are authoritative, not rounded JavaScript Date. If item expires during viewing, next fresh read may remove it; this is a forecast, not an immutable historical receipt. A missing expiry is not an expiry forecast.

### API, SQL ownership, cursor and consistency contract
- **Nest endpoints (proposed):** authenticated/consent/CSRF owner-only POST /api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/summary with {windowDays:7|30}; POST /api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/day with {kstDate:YYYY-MM-DD,limit?:20|50,cursor?:opaque}. Derive actor from session; never accept owner ID. Next server boundary and Android /app-api/v1/shop/expiry-calendar/* use identical validated schemas. Request body <=2KiB; proposed 20 owner reads/minute with separate burst cap to measure. Strict date must be within selected 30-day horizon. 200 with {status:'VERIFIED',asOfUtc,timeZone:'Asia/Seoul',windowDays,days:[{kstDate,typeCount,unitCount,earliestExpiryUtc}],totalTypes,totalUnits} and day {status:'VERIFIED',kstDate,asOfUtc,items,nextCursor?,totalTypes,totalUnits}; verified empty is 200 only after authoritative query. 400 invalid/oversize, 401 unauthenticated, 403 consent/CSRF, 409 STALE_DAY, 429 quota, 503 DB/schema/ACL/unknown. No caching or fallback-to-empty.
- **DB boundary:** forward-only owner-scoped SECURITY DEFINER functions (provisional shop_owner_expiry_calendar_summary_v1(actor,window_days) and shop_owner_expiry_calendar_day_v1(actor,kst_date,limit,cursor_fields)); fixed search_path, migrator ownership, explicit EXECUTE to moneyverse_app only. Never GRANT direct SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on user_items, shop_catalog, receipt, identity, or finance tables. Use one primary-DB statement snapshot and one DB asOf for each response; do not pretend separate HTTP requests share a snapshot. Join catalog by UUID after filtering owner; no arbitrary client SQL. Index candidate (user_id,expires_at,catalog_id) WHERE quantity>0 AND expires_at IS NOT NULL only after EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS) on 10,001 synthetic holdings and insert-cost review. No new table needed in V1. Type counts are COUNT(*) bigint for distinct owner+catalog PK rows, unit counts SUM(quantity)::bigint, serialized as exact decimal strings if outside JS safe integer range.
- **Stable day pagination:** default 20/max 50, ordered by (expires_at ASC,catalog_id ASC). An opaque HMAC cursor binds actor, KST date, last exact-microsecond expiry and UUID, complete-day deterministic fingerprint over sorted (catalog_id,exact expiry,quantity), schema version, issuedAt and 120-second expiry. A new day read recomputes fingerprint on one statement snapshot; if changed or cursor expired, return 409 STALE_DAY and refresh, never silently claim a complete stable result. Cursor must not embed item names or session secrets; rotate signing key. Fingerprint/EXPLAIN cost and max response size are acceptance gates, not assumed acceptable. Do not use acquired_at as holding-generation evidence. If fingerprint or cursor verification cannot be implemented safely, keep flag OFF; no fake nextCursor.
- **Privacy and operational boundaries:** Cache-Control private,no-store; X-Robots-Tag noindex; Referrer-Policy no-referrer on all 200/4xx/5xx at Nest, Next, Android gateway, and page. Vary Cookie when appropriate; no sitemap, crawler indexing, query-string item IDs, raw owner item names in analytics or admin. Protect against cross-account response reuse and parameter tampering; CSRF and same-origin/session boundaries. No write transactions, no reminder preference changes, no ledger/WLD/holdings mutations. Any operator metrics aggregate >=20 members only; day-view, empty, retry, stale cursor, 429/503, p95 latency and 7/30 conversion are proposed KPIs. p95<300ms is an unmeasured target, not a result.

### Source findings, engineering backlog, QA and release
- **Source-backed:** migration 071 user_items has PRIMARY KEY(user_id,catalog_id), quantity>=0, expires_at timestamptz, and revoked app grants. Migration 123 shop_my_items_v2 is owner-scoped SECURITY DEFINER and filters quantity>0 plus future expiry; it also includes nonexpiring items and samples clock_timestamp, so its existing response is not a consistent 30-day aggregate. Next /inventory/page.tsx uses apiOrNull and falls back to [] on upstream failure; the new calendar must not copy that false-empty behavior. Latest main still has no F675-199 SQL/API/page; do not report feature as implemented. Separate from A/B/C/QA and mass-integration Draft #2206.
- **P0 OPS1572-01** (#1984/#2144/#2171): executable/backend/frontend/edge SHA provenance, cgroup headroom and independent restore/rollback.
- **P0 SEC1572-02** (#993/#2111): clean PG17 app ACL/checksum and read-only owner isolation, exact time and query cost; no direct table grants.
- **P0 FIN1572-03** (#1976/#2153/#2191/#2209): Treasury/marketplace financial source truth, unledgered paths and fabricated appraisal; calendar never changes WLD/ledger.
- **P0 REL1572-04** (#1088/#2206): reconcile concurrent integration/QA changes, full security/audit, exact candidate SHA official Test authenticated E2E, independent restore and explicit operator release.

## v2026.10.30.1512 — F675-184 Member Inventory Find & Sort (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Previous / Current / Next:** Feature Improvement v1510 / Feature Addition v1512 / Feature Improvement v1514 (provisional). Authority origin/main 9da6545c4ff4809b5bd84ab6a28b9d2f1db74cef rechecked at start and mid; stacked after planning Draft #2008 (which follows #2003/#1995/#1990/#1983); development handoff #2013; Draft PR #2014. English canonical; Korean meaning-equivalent. Documentation-only proposal, not an implemented or approved design. No separate distributed feature plan.

### Verified product gap, source and design alternatives
- Current frontend/src/app/inventory/page.tsx requires a member and fetches GET /api/v1/shop/holdings through apiOrNull. The client inventory-view.tsx has only category tabs, no keyword/rarity/equipped filter or acquisition/name sorting. It displays an empty inventory when the upstream returns null; this can misrepresent an outage as a genuine empty holding set. Current equip POST remains separate and is not part of this feature.
- Nest ShopController.holdings delegates the authenticated actor to ShopCatalogRepository.holdings, which reads public.shop_my_items_v2(actor) from migration 123. The SECURITY DEFINER function returns owner items with quantity > 0 and unexpired held rows, ordered by acquired_at DESC, catalog_id; it also exposes rarity, equipped, expiry, arrears and suspended status. Its app-role EXECUTE grant does not authorize direct table reads. Passing actor UUID alone is not independent DB identity authentication: Nest session and consent must bind the actor. This source does NOT prove Production row counts. A further READ ONLY DEV PostgreSQL 17.11 check found effective moneyverse_app direct SELECT=true and DELETE=true on public.user_items despite function EXECUTE=true (6 DEV rows, aggregate only). This contradicts intended least privilege and blocks rollout under P0 #993; it does NOT prove Production permissions or compromise.
- Alternative A, client-side filtering of the unbounded current holdings payload, is simple but cannot bound network/CPU for 10,001+ holdings and inherits the false-empty behavior. Alternative B, new search table/materialized index, creates unnecessary sync and migration risk. **Chosen V1 proposal: a bounded, read-only owner-scoped SQL function and typed search endpoint, with no new table and no financial mutation.** It depends on a forward-only migration sequenced after Backend B's existing 307–311 stack; no migration number is reserved here.

### Purpose, audience, permissions, entry and UX
- Purpose: help an authenticated, consent-current member find owned cosmetics/items without scanning an entire inventory. Entry /inventory, new labelled Find items search input, Search/Clear CTA, existing category tabs, rarity dropdown (all/common/uncommon/rare/epic/legendary/mythic only when represented by source), Equipped-only toggle and sort Recent first / Oldest first / Name A–Z. Preserve avatar preview and equip/un-equip actions; the search endpoint itself is GET-only and never equips, purchases, pays upkeep, mints or transfers WLD.
- Filter defaults: q empty, category all, rarity all, equipped all, sort recent, page size 20 (hard maximum 50). Search q is trimmed Unicode 2–40 code points when nonempty; literal substring matching, not regex; escape LIKE wildcard %, _ and backslash, reject control characters, duplicate parameters, unknown enum, oversize input and malformed UTF-8. Normalize filters identically on Nest/Next/Android; no hidden global catalogue results. Preserve input on 400 and provide a clear correction.
- States: initial (existing unfiltered view), loading, verified results, verified empty search (not zero owned), filter reset, in-flight account switch, source changed (409 with explicit Refresh), expired cursor (410 Restart), rate-limited (429), unavailable (503 with Retry), offline, unauthorized and consent expired. A source error must never become holdings=[] or a success-shaped count; do not silently mix stale equipped showcase with fresh search results. Page count and exact total are omitted unless verified in the same read transaction.
- Mobile/a11y: 320px layout, 200% zoom, 44px targets, WCAG 2.2 AA, visible labels, keyboard Enter search, tab/focus recovery after pagination and errors, aria-live status without focus theft, reduced motion, Korean/English strings, screen reader announces verified result count on current page. No autosubmit on each keystroke.

### API, DB invariants, pagination and concurrency
- Nest GET /api/v1/shop/holdings/search?q=&category=&rarity=&equipped=&sort=&limit=&cursor=; authenticated/consented actor only (SessionGuard, AuthenticatedGuard, ConsentGuard). Next private server BFF forwards allowlisted query keys through server-only API helper; Android GET /app-api/v1/shop/holdings/search uses existing authenticated gateway and generated contract parity. Return {items:[existing HeldItem DTO],pageSize,hasMore,nextCursor,sourceStatus:'VERIFIED',asOfUtc}; never return another owner's items or raw audit/financial details. Error codes 400 invalid, 401 unauthenticated, 403 consent, 409 changed source, 410 expired, 429 rate, 503 DB/source; foreign IDs are not accepted.
- DB: new reviewed forward-only public.shop_my_items_search_v1(p_actor uuid, p_query text, p_category text, p_rarity text, p_equipped boolean, p_sort text, p_limit integer, p_after_* cursor keys) SECURITY DEFINER, stable within one read-only REPEATABLE READ request, fixed search_path, schema-qualified relations, owner WHERE held.user_id=p_actor, quantity>0, expiry>asOf, same arrears/preview semantics as shop_my_items_v2. Revokes PUBLIC EXECUTE, grants app role EXECUTE only, reasserts no direct SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on user_items, shop_catalog, shop_upkeep_arrears and receipts. No new table, foreign key, balance change or mutable transaction. Existing PK/FK/quantity and expiry constraints stay authoritative. Review indexes (user_id, acquired_at DESC, catalog_id DESC) and (user_id, catalog_id) plus catalogue category/rarity and lower(name) with EXPLAIN/BUFFERS on 10,001 seeded rows; only add justified nonduplicate indexes in coordinated forward migration.
- Stable keyset: recent/oldest uses acquired_at microseconds + catalog_id UUID; name uses lower(name) COLLATE C + catalog_id UUID, never locale-unstable OFFSET. HMAC-SHA256 cursor with purpose/version, owner, session generation, normalized filter/sort, asOf UTC microseconds, last keys, expiry <=15 minutes. Signature, actor, sort, filter or session mismatch -> 400/409; expired -> 410. HTTP requests do not share an MVCC snapshot. Re-evaluate an owner-scoped source-set revision/fingerprint for each page; changed eligible holdings/equip/expiry -> 409 REFRESH_REQUIRED rather than promise immutable results. If full fingerprint exceeds p95 300ms TARGET at 10,001 rows, block feature rollout and redesign revision strategy; never label an unverified page complete. Limit 50+1 and bounded SQL timeout/rate budget.
- No idempotency key or write transaction on GET; equip/purchase/upkeep retain their existing independently authenticated, CSRF/idempotency-protected write paths. New search must not bypass those guards. Android must cancel in-flight requests and discard responses on logout/account switch; no local disk caching.

### Admin, abuse, privacy, SEO, analytics and deployment
- Privacy: Cache-Control private,no-store and X-Robots-Tag noindex,nofollow plus no-referrer on success/errors, no sitemap/canonical search pages, no indexed private search query URLs. Confirm HTTP response headers, not only Next metadata, in light of Production private-route header contradiction #2012. Do not log q, item names, owner UUID, signed cursor or raw response; rate-limit per authenticated actor and bound query CPU, memory and payload. No administrator individual inventory search in V1.
- Admin KPI: aggregate-only weekly adoption, verified search completion, empty-result rate, 400/409/410/429/503, p95 latency, filter usage and account-switch stale-response drops, suppressed for cohorts below 20 distinct members; no raw query text or member identifiers. p95 <300ms, no cross-owner disclosures and zero ledger writes are acceptance TARGETS, not observed measurements.
- Feature flag inventory_find_sort defaults OFF. Developer B/C/A/QA use separate branch/test Docker, coordinate SQL numbering and contract. Test exact candidate SHA for frontend/backend/edge/Android with authenticated owner E2E, all required CI, security, negative grants, independent backup restore and finance invariants before approval. Rollout OFF -> staff cohort -> limited cohort -> monitor -> broader only after sign-off; rollback OFF preserves existing category tabs/equip flow and does not delete holdings, receipts or indexes. Production promotion is BLOCKED until all P0 gates pass; planning never deploys.

### P0/P1 developer backlog — 4 P0 + 6 P1
1. **P0 OPS1512-01** — #1984 Production advertised SHA 94d38f4 vs old deleted process path; prove executable/edge manifest, rollback artifacts and independent restore before restart or release.

6. **P1 INVENTORY1512-06** — B typed Nest GET, query allowlist, HMAC cursor and 400/401/403/409/410/429/503 fail-closed source/error contract, resource limits.
7. **P1 INVENTORY1512-07** — A/C Next inventory Find/Clear/rarity/equipped/sort, preserved category/equip flows, verified-empty vs unavailable, keyboard/a11y/320px.

**Acceptance PROPOSED, NOT RUN.** Confirm source-equivalent item visibility, unexpired boundary, correct rarity and stable microsecond ordering, source-change 409, invalid/missing vs verified empty, cross-owner denial, HTTP privacy headers and default-OFF fallback. No runtime/DB/WLD/ledger/Test/Production change; DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD.


## v2026.10.30.1510 — F675-183 Weekly Quest Evidence Canonical-Parity Hardening (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Previous / Current / Next:** Feature Addition v1508 / Feature Improvement v1510 / Feature Addition v1512 (provisional). Main SHA 9da6545c4ff4809b5bd84ab6a28b9d2f1db74cef rechecked start/mid. Docs-only successor to Draft #2003, stacked on #1995 → #1990 → #1983; existing handoff #2002; Draft #2008. Authority main AGENTS.md, README.md, English canonical and Korean equivalent. No separate feature planning file.

### Verified gaps against migration 101 — parity gate before implementation
- The canonical public.early_game_weekly_goals(p_actor) in packages/database/migrations/101-early-game-progress.sql:437–566 computes the KST week with clock_timestamp(), but applies only created_at >= v_from to receipts and ledger transactions: **no next-Monday upper bound and no shared asOf cutoff**. The proposed [Monday, next Monday) detail can disagree for future-dated/backfilled rows or week rollover. Require same-transaction oracle equality for all four metrics; if the stricter bound is desired, update canonical and detail together through a separately reviewed forward-only migration. Never rewrite applied 101.
- Current job is highest-level user_job_progress ordered by level DESC, job_type (enum tie-break), NOT selected_at or job at receipt time. Distinct work counts DISTINCT assignment.task_id; job work counts paid work_reward_receipts whose task job equals the current highest-level job. A grouped task evidence row is not one receipt; changing job rank may change old weekly progress without a new receipt.
- Spend is only USER_CASH credit postings for SHOP_CATALOG_PURCHASE, SHOP_PURCHASE, BUSINESS_PURCHASE, CONSUMPTION_EVENT. Savings is USER_BANK debit minus credit for BANK_DEPOSIT and BANK_WITHDRAW, clamped with GREATEST(net,0). The canonical 101 query does not explicitly filter accounts.currency='WLD'; a new WLD-only detail must prove parity or coordinate a canonical change. A 50-row page cannot be summed into the full progress.
- NPC affinity is lifetime MAX(npc_relationships.affinity), self_reported=true: pressing the NPC order button is not a verified delivery. Return AGGREGATE_ONLY / SELF_REPORTED, no invented receipt, event time or verified-weekly badge.

### Corrected owner-only V1 contract
- **Purpose, audience, entry:** Authenticated/consented member can explain their own current quest board, never claim reward or certify settlement. /quests card CTA View evidence → /quests/weekly-evidence?goal=<active-catalog-code>&week=<current-KST-Monday>. NPC uses the week parameter only as board context and prominently labels its window lifetime. Feature switch quest_weekly_evidence default OFF; no historical archive, exports, cross-owner or administrator receipt browsing.
- **Snapshot and state:** Obtain DB KST week and asOfUtc once. In one read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction compare canonical 101 goal_code, metric, window, target, progress, self_reported and the new detail aggregate. Only identical results earn sourceStatus=CANONICAL_MATCHED; otherwise 503 PARITY_UNVERIFIED without success-shaped zero/rows. Week rollover yields 409 WEEK_CHANGED + Refresh. An MVCC snapshot cannot be held across HTTP pages.
- **Cursor:** Versioned purpose-separated HMAC-SHA256 (15m) binds actor, session epoch, goal, week, formula/catalog revision, current highest-level job, asOfUtc microseconds, full eligible source-set fingerprint, stable last (timestamp, UUID/group-key) and expiry. 50+1 keyset, max 50; distinct-task groups need deterministic tie-breaks. Recompute fingerprint over ALL eligible rows, not only visible page. Backfill/deletion/job change → 409 EVIDENCE_CHANGED; expired → 410. If 10,001-row fingerprint exceeds p95 <300ms seeded Test target, BLOCK performance gate and redesign; never promise stable pages from cutoff alone.
- **API and UI:** Nest GET /api/v1/engagement/early-game/weekly-evidence and Android GET /app-api/v1/engagement/early-game/weekly-evidence. Typed result {goalCode,weekStartKst,windowKind,weekEndExclusiveUtc,metric,target,progress,selfReported,sourceStatus,evidenceStatus,asOfUtcMicros,rows,nextCursor}. Exact decimal strings for BIGINT/WLD and UTC microseconds. Rows are partial evidence, not additive totals. NPC returns no list/cursor. Typed 400 invalid, 401 auth, 404 foreign/missing indistinguishable, 409 changed, 410 expired, 429 rate, 503 source/parity/DB. Loading, verified empty, aggregate-only, changed, retry and unavailable must never fabricate a completed goal.
- **DB and abuse controls:** SECURITY DEFINER owner-scoped read, qualified relations, fixed search_path, revoke PUBLIC EXECUTE, minimum app EXECUTE, negative direct DML/SELECT tests, EXPLAIN/BUFFERS before indexes. p_actor argument alone is NOT DB identity proof: Nest session/consent actor binding and least privilege are required. No new table in V1. No private UUID/transaction logs, no-store/noindex/no-referrer on success and errors, session-switch cancellation and no Android disk cache, 320px/200% zoom, 44px touch, WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard/focus recovery.
- **Admin and release:** Admin sees only anonymous aggregate KPI when >=20 distinct members: opens, aggregate-only, parity-fail, changed, 503, p95. No individual evidence or searchable member IDs. p95 <300ms is a TARGET, NOT MEASURED. Separate developer branch/test Docker; full CI, exact-head official Test frontend/backend/edge authenticated E2E, independent restore and finance/security gates. Default OFF → limited cohort → observe → OFF rollback without ledger/data deletion. Planning never deploys.

## v2026.10.30.1508 — F675-183 Member Weekly Quest Evidence Breakdown (FEATURE ADDITION / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Previous / Current / Next Cycle Type:** Feature Improvement v1506 / Feature Addition v1508 / Feature Improvement v1510 (provisional). Start and mid-run origin/main `9da6545c4ff4809b5bd84ab6a28b9d2f1db74cef`; planning-only stacked on unmerged Draft #1995 → #1990 → #1983. [P0/P1 handoff #2002](https://github.com/wtrdd1-hash/Woldeok-Moneyverse-Migration/issues/2002). Canonical requirements: AGENTS.md, README.md, this English PROJECT_PLAN.md; Korean equivalent PROJECT_PLAN.ko.md.

### Product rationale, existing evidence and non-overlap
- **Observed:** `frontend/src/app/quests/page.tsx` renders four early-game weekly goal cards from `GET /api/v1/engagement/early-game`. `packages/database/migrations/101-early-game-progress.sql` computes goals from verified work_reward_receipts, eligible ledger postings and NPC relationship affinity, but the UI exposes no drilldown showing why a weekly figure moved. This is separate from wallet transaction detail F675-182, calendar range F675-181, saved filters and Android banking pocket read work; no code is implemented in this planning cycle.
- **Purpose/target:** Give authenticated, consented members a transparent read-only explanation of their own current-week quest progress without allowing self-awarded rewards or creating an alternate financial balance. Success: members can trace contributing activity, distinguish aggregated from receipt-level evidence, and never see fabricated empty or zero progress on API failure.
- **V1 scope:** Current KST Monday–Sunday week only; no historical archive, exports, reward claims, transaction changes, profile disclosure or administrator access to individual receipts. Four metric kinds: `distinct_work_tasks` (unique work task IDs, not raw receipt count), `job_work_completions` (verified work receipts matching the user's selected job rule), `spend_or_save` (eligible cash spending + max(0, bank deposits minus withdrawals), WLD exact integer), and `npc_affinity` (current relationship aggregate only, no invented events). Preserve the exact eligibility/type allowlist in migration 101; do not treat gambling, stock buys or arbitrary debits as consumption.

### Permissions, entry, screens and CTA
- **Entry:** On `/quests` weekly goal cards, a visible `근거 보기 / View evidence` CTA links to `/quests/weekly-evidence?goal=<catalog-code>&week=<YYYY-MM-DD>`. Server-side `requireMember` and session/consent verification precede all data access; feature switch `quest_weekly_evidence` default OFF. Only catalogued goal codes; no raw SQL identifiers or arbitrary dates.
- **Screen:** Goal label, canonical KST week range, target/progress as exact decimal strings, metric explanation, evidence source and limitation, bounded list of contributing rows (timestamp, category, safe label, signed contribution where meaningful), and Back/Retry/Next page. For distinct-work counts, show unique task grouping; do not add row amounts to infer the total. For spend-or-save, show eligible spending and signed bank deposits/withdrawals, net-clamp explanation; no full counterparty identities. For NPC affinity show `AGGREGATE_ONLY`, no receipt list and a truthful note.
- **States:** LOADING, READY_WITH_ROWS, VERIFIED_EMPTY, AGGREGATE_ONLY, EVIDENCE_CHANGED (refresh required), INVALID_REQUEST, UNAUTHENTICATED, UNAVAILABLE and RATE_LIMITED. A failed read never renders zero, success or a reward receipt. On an expired cursor, offer Refresh without silently dropping filters. 320px mobile, semantic table/list, focus recovery, 44px controls, keyboard and screen-reader status announcements, WCAG 2.2 AA.

### API, database, exactness and transaction boundaries
- **API:** `GET /api/v1/engagement/early-game/weekly-evidence?goal=<code>&week=<date>&cursor=<opaque>` and Android parity `GET /app-api/v1/engagement/early-game/weekly-evidence`. Success: `{goalCode, weekStartKst, weekEndExclusiveUtc, metric, target, progress, sourceStatus, evidenceStatus, asOfUtc, rows, nextCursor}`. Money/counts serialized as canonical base-10 strings; timestamps retain PostgreSQL microseconds. Explicit typed 400 invalid goal/week, 401 unauthenticated, 404 not found/foreign indistinguishable, 409 EVIDENCE_CHANGED, 410 expired cursor, 429 throttled, 503 unavailable. No caching or success-shaped fallback. GET is read-only; all mutation methods rejected.
- **DB contract:** New reviewed `SECURITY DEFINER` owner-scoped read function(s) only if needed, schema-qualified relations, pinned search_path, PUBLIC EXECUTE revoked, only necessary app-role EXECUTE granted, no direct table DML/SELECT relaxation. `p_actor` is NOT an independent DB identity proof: Nest session binding and separately reviewed app-role least privilege are mandatory. No new table for V1; add index only after `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on a disposable seeded DB demonstrates need. Candidate indexes: work_reward_receipts(user_id,created_at,id), work_assignments(id,task_id), ledger_transactions(created_at,id), ledger_postings(account_id,transaction_id), account owner/type; check existing indexes before proposing migration.
- **Consistency:** Use a single read-only REPEATABLE READ DB transaction to calculate canonical summary and first page from one snapshot. Later pages bind actor, goal, KST week, as-of UTC, last key, expiry and a server-computed canonical source-row fingerprint in HMAC-signed cursor (15 min). Recompute fingerprint before later pages; any backfill, deletion, job-selection or NPC-affinity change returns 409 rather than silently mixing snapshots. Stable keyset ordering (`created_at DESC, stable UUID`); 50+1 per page, hard max 50; server must not hold a long-lived transaction between HTTP requests. If full fingerprint is too expensive, fail the performance gate and redesign before implementation; do not promise stable pagination without proof.
- **Correctness/security:** KST Monday 00:00 inclusive to next Monday 00:00 exclusive; no client clock trust, future week, or timezone ambiguity. Apply the same source cutoff and job selection as migration 101. DB BIGINT/NUMERIC never coerced through JS Number; protect UUIDs and raw identifiers in telemetry. Rate-limit by actor/session/IP, bounded statement timeout, input allowlist, deny cross-owner, no CSRF write path, anti-enumeration 404, no-store/noindex/no-referrer on success and errors. Android session-switch cancellation and private no-disk-cache parity.

### Operations, administration, KPI, release and rollback
- **Admin:** Aggregate-only feature adoption and failure rate, minimum 20 distinct members before displaying cohorts, no individual quest/ledger rows or searchable user IDs. Metrics: `quest_evidence_open_total`, `quest_evidence_verified_empty_total`, `quest_evidence_aggregate_only_total`, `quest_evidence_changed_total`, `quest_evidence_api_error_total`, `quest_evidence_p95_ms`. Proposed p95 <300ms on seeded Test is a target, not a measured result. No public SEO indexing; private routes use noindex/nofollow and private no-store.
- **Safe rollout:** Feature flag OFF until isolated PostgreSQL, security/contract/a11y/mobile, exact-SHA official Test frontend/backend/edge/auth and independent restore gates pass. Development in separate branch/worktree/test Docker; reviewed forward-only migration only if required, no applied checksum rewrite. Stage canary by member cohort, monitor 409/503/p95, rollback flag OFF and code to prior verified SHA without deleting evidence or ledger records. No planning-run runtime deployment.
- **Acceptance proposed, NOT EXECUTED:** >=10,001 synthetic receipts/postings, 100 cross-owner, 100 cursor tamper, 100 concurrent, 50 snapshot/backfill/late-commit races, 30 KST Monday/leap/year boundaries, 50 invalid/timeout responses, NPC aggregate-only, distinct-count non-additivity, net-withdrawal clamp, zero WLD/ledger mutation, full frontend/backend regressions and real Android gateway contract. All numbers are test design targets, not passed tests.

## v2026.10.30.1506 — F675-182 Wallet Detail Evidence Hardening (FEATURE IMPROVEMENT / DRAFT / RELEASE HOLD)

**Previous / Current / Next Cycle Type:** Feature Addition v1504 / Feature Improvement v1506 / Feature Addition v1508 (provisional). Main 9da6545c4ff4809b5bd84ab6a28b9d2f1db74cef checked start and midpoint. AGENTS.md, README, English canonical PROJECT_PLAN.md and Korean parity reviewed. Documentation-only successor stacked on unmerged Draft #1990 → #1983; existing engineering handoff #1988. No duplicate feature, runtime/DB/WLD/Test/Production writes.

**Source-backed design correction:** Existing wallet.repository.ts aggregates ledger postings by account.owner_user_id, but wallet.service.ts converts PostgreSQL timestamps through JS Date, losing microseconds. No detail route exists in main. Accounts currency is char(3), posting amount positive bigint. Detail SQL must explicitly filter owner USER_CASH/USER_BANK currency WLD, include historical frozen/closed accounts, sum signed NUMERIC exactly and return canonical integer strings. netDelta=cashDelta+bankDelta; zero net does not alone prove internal transfer. Only allowlisted authoritative bank-move type plus opposite pocket deltas may be called an internal move. Preserve original UTC microseconds separately from KST display. Type label must come from a safe server allowlist.

**Security limitation:** SECURITY DEFINER with p_actor does NOT independently authenticate the SQL caller. A compromised app role could invoke EXECUTE with another actor UUID without a separately proven DB-bound identity mechanism; DEV role also has direct ledger SELECT. Require Nest authenticated session/consent-to-actor binding, review auth_sessions id/user_id/expires_at/revoked_at and limits, independent least-privilege DB verification. A forgeable GUC is not an identity proof. Fixed search_path, qualified public tables, dedicated function owner, REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC and reviewed app EXECUTE only. No new direct table grants. One statement snapshot; EXPLAIN existing indexes before new ones.

**Evidence semantics:** Successful owner ledger SELECT means row retrieval only, NOT globally reconciled postings, payment finality, certified receipt, live balance or verified settlement. Supersede ambiguous LEDGER_READ_VERIFIED with readStatus=READ_OK and reconciliationStatus=NOT_ASSESSED. UI says “원장 기록 조회됨 · 정산 검증서 아님”. Do not fabricate zero or counterpart data; inconsistent currency/amount/posting source must fail closed (503). Absent/foreign identical 404, malformed UUID 400, unauthenticated 401, throttled 429, unavailable 503.

**Member UX/API:** /wallet/activity “거래 상세 보기” to private /wallet/activity/transactions/:transactionId; Nest GET /api/v1/wallet/activity/transactions/:transactionId and Android /app-api/v1/wallet/activity/transactions/:transactionId. 200 strict DTO {transactionId,typeLabel,occurredAtUtcMicros,cashDelta,bankDelta,netDelta,currency:'WLD',readStatus:'READ_OK',reconciliationStatus:'NOT_ASSESSED'}. Validate unknown JSON, no URL actor, allowlisted Back filters, loading/empty-not-found/error/retry/copy/focus states. Session switching cancels stale requests. Private no-store, noindex, no-referrer on success and errors, no sitemap/ID logs. WCAG 2.2 AA, 320px, 200% zoom, 44px controls, semantic definition list and aria-live. Admin anonymous >=20-member cohort detail_open/unavailable/p95 KPI only. Default OFF wallet_transaction_detail_v1. Backward-compatible migration only by separate developer branch; feature-OFF rollback never deletes ledger/backups.

## Central Bank / Mint / Treasury institutional separation — v2026.10.04.523 (2026-10-04)

- **Authority decision:** Moneyverse economic authority is separated into Moneyverse Central Bank (monetary-policy approval), Moneyverse Mint Bureau (execution-only mint/retire), Central Treasury (tax/budget/expenditure of existing WLD), and Economy Core & Settlement Ledger (double-entry settlement/reconciliation/invariants).
- **Supply invariant:** taxes, transfers, treasury budgets, treasury spending, deposits, withdrawals, funded loans, trades and vault movement do not change total WLD supply. Only a canonical authorized mint or retirement changes supply.
- **Treasury reserve semantics:** existing protected treasury reserves are fiscal-liquidity reserves and do not authorize currency creation. A fiscal shortfall cannot silently become a mint.
- **Debt/banking:** Treasury bonds redistribute existing WLD and initial bank lending stays fully funded from existing WLD pools; commercial-bank deposit-money creation is intentionally excluded until a separately approved monetary-layer design exists.
- **AI boundary:** AI may diagnose/simulate/recommend within current bounded policy rules, but cannot create/approve monetary orders, execute Mint, or convert treasury shortage into issuance.
- **Migration/release gate:** classify every WLD increase/burn path, split ambiguous injection semantics, preserve historical ledger records, prove independent supply and treasury reconciliation, and require exact-SHA isolated Test evidence before zero-downtime Production promotion.
- **Detailed authority:** [Central Bank, Mint, Treasury & Economy Core Specification v523](CENTRAL_BANK_MINT_TREASURY_ECONOMY_CORE_SPEC.md).
- **Evidence boundary:** v523 is planning/documentation only. It does not claim runtime, DB, Test or Production implementation.

## P0/P1 database architecture integrity and scale contract — v2026.09.25.443 (2026-09-25)

- **Evidence breadth without false certainty:** a Crossref discovery run collected 80,000 raw records across ten database-architecture lanes and produced **66,858 deduplicated candidates** using DOI first and normalized-title fallback. This is a discovery corpus, not a claim that every candidate was manually reviewed or database-specific. Production requirements below use directly checked PostgreSQL 17 primary documentation and current repository evidence.
- **Preserve the current authority boundary:** numbered SQL migrations remain schema authority; applied migrations remain immutable/checksummed; the runtime application role remains non-owner/no-DDL; protected economic writes continue through reviewed PostgreSQL transaction/function boundaries with exact integer money and business idempotency.
- **P0 schema fingerprint/drift gate:** every exact candidate must be able to rebuild an empty PostgreSQL 17 database and generate a normalized manifest of columns/types/defaults/nullability, PK/UNIQUE/FK/CHECK constraints, indexes, triggers, routines/security-definer search paths, ownership/grants and migration checksums. Test/Production catalog drift that cannot be explained by migration history blocks acceptance.
- **P0 key/constraint/FK-index audit:** canonical tables require a PK or explicit reviewed keyless exception. Domain invariants belong in DB constraints where safely expressible. Because PostgreSQL does not automatically index referencing FK columns, every child FK requires a suitable supporting left-prefix index or a measured/documented exception.
- **P0 zero-downtime schema evolution:** nontrivial migrations use expand -> optional compatible dual period -> bounded resumable backfill -> low-blocking index/constraint build/validation -> switch -> old-runtime retirement -> later contract. Each migration records lock/scan/rewrite class and forward-fix/rollback semantics; destructive/table-rewrite work is first exercised on representative isolated Test data.
- **P0 concurrency correctness:** retryable serialization/deadlock failures retry the **whole transaction logic** with bounded backoff while preserving the business idempotency identity. Deterministic lock ordering remains mandatory for multi-account/entity mutations.
- **P0 ledger reconciliation:** append-only balanced postings remain the economic audit authority. Mutable balance projections must update atomically and provide sampled/full reconciliation plus a controlled rebuild/repair path; historical postings are corrected by new reversal/correction transactions, not mutation/deletion.
- **P1 measured index/partition lifecycle:** index creation/removal is tied to real query predicates, PostgreSQL statistics and representative `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`. Partitioning is allowed only for measured large/growing/retention-heavy tables with a decision record; audit/outbox/chat/price/telemetry history are candidates, not automatically partitioned.
- **P1 typed core and lifecycle semantics:** authoritative identity, money, ownership, lifecycle state, idempotency and timestamps stay typed/constrained columns. JSONB is bounded to versioned flexible payloads. Every FK intentionally selects delete behavior so ledger/audit/financial history cannot disappear through accidental cascade.
- **P1 maintenance/observability:** monitor autovacuum/analyze freshness, dead tuples/XID pressure, long transactions, blocking/deadlocks/serialization retries, relation/index growth, temp spill, invalid/duplicate/unused-index candidates and approved `pg_stat_statements` query evidence. Routine `VACUUM FULL` is not normal maintenance.
- **P0/P1 recovery evolution:** keep the verified encrypted logical-backup path; it is not PITR. Stronger RPO/RTO requires independently stored base backups/WAL archives, immutable off-host failure domain and a disposable restore drill proving timestamp recovery, lineage and application integrity before acceptance.
- **No architecture-by-corpus:** v443 does not authorize an ORM migration takeover, blanket partitioning, generic sharding/distributed SQL, or a PostgreSQL major upgrade. Current runtime remains PostgreSQL 17-compatible unless a separate upgrade is planned and validated.
- Detailed authority: [DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md](DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md) and [database architecture research review](../findings/MONEYVERSE_DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE_RESEARCH_REVIEW_v2026.09.25.443.md). This cycle is planning/research/docs only; no schema/Test/Production change is claimed.

Any newly added page is automatically in scope.
- **No silent exclusions:** every discovered route must have PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED evidence. A missing ledger row, skipped page, “not changed”, “looks similar”, or historical pass is not acceptance evidence. Any intentional non-release surface still requires an explicit classification and direct rendering check.
- **Dynamic pages:** every dynamic route requires deterministic valid fixtures plus invalid/not-found/permission cases where applicable. QA may not satisfy `[id]`, `[symbol]`, `[clubId]` or equivalent routes by checking only their parent list page.
- **Authentication/role matrix:** exercise each page in every materially distinct state it supports: guest, signed-in member, restricted/permission-denied, owner/non-owner where relevant, and administrator/privileged roles. Redirects and access-denied behavior count as page behavior and must be verified.
- **All sections and controls:** opening a route is not enough. Scroll header-to-footer, visit every tab/accordion/section, open relevant dialogs/drawers, exercise primary and secondary controls, and verify navigation back/forward and refresh persistence where stateful.
- **Responsive full-site matrix:** the v440 viewport contract applies to **every page**, not only modified/admin pages: 320/360/375/390/412/430 portrait, representative landscape, 768/1024 tablet, desktop, plus 200% and applicable 400% zoom/reflow. Body overflow, clipping, overlap, hidden CTA, inaccessible control, or lost decision-critical content is a failure.
- **Five complete full-site QA cycles:** every release candidate receives at least **five complete passes over the entire discovered page inventory**. Every pass must include every page; the combined five-pass evidence must cover the required viewport/state matrix, long/short content, loading/empty/partial/error states and real API-populated data. Fixes found during a pass require rerunning the affected page and all dependent shared-layout/component coverage.
- **Administrator baseline:** all `/admin/**` routes are verified in each full-site pass with authenticated administrator runtime data, including navigation, forms, tables/cards, dialogs, destructive/sensitive actions in safe Test mode, role/step-up behavior, audit evidence and responsive layout. “Admin checked separately later” is prohibited.
- **State surfaces:** route QA includes loading/skeleton, empty, long-content, partial/stale, validation failure, network/server error, offline/maintenance where supported, permission denied, success and mutation pending/retry states. A page that only passes with happy-path seeded data is not accepted.
- **Runtime truth:** Test QA runs against the exact candidate SHA and real backend/API/database contracts. Mock-only, screenshot-only, source inspection, unit tests, or a previous release’s browser run cannot replace route-by-route runtime evidence.
- **Coverage gate:** discovered-page count = QA-ledger distinct-page count = pages with final accepted evidence. Any count mismatch, unresolved FAIL/BLOCKED, console/runtime error attributable to the candidate, or administrator-page gap blocks Production promotion.
- **Evidence:** retain exact SHA, generated route inventory hash/count, route, role/state, fixture ID, browser/engine, viewport/orientation/zoom, pass number, API/runtime identity, result and defect linkage. This evidence is required for Test acceptance and Production promotion.
- Detailed authority: [FULL_ROUTE_UI_QA_SPEC.md](FULL_ROUTE_UI_QA_SPEC.md) and [ACCESSIBILITY_RESPONSIVE_INTERACTION_SPEC.md](ACCESSIBILITY_RESPONSIVE_INTERACTION_SPEC.md). v442 is planning/documentation only; it does not claim that all current pages have already passed this new gate.

## P0 economy-admin canonical control-state contract — v2026.09.25.441 (2026-09-25)

- **One canonical value envelope:** each tunable economy control is rendered from one server-derived object containing current persisted value, unit, min/max/step, policy/source version, ownership mode (`AUTO`/`MANUAL_OVERRIDE`), proposed value if any, updated-at and loading/error state. Independent frontend defaults are prohibited.
- **Zero is data, not fallback:** missing/loading/failed policy data must render `loading`, `unknown` or `blocked`; the client must never substitute `0`, `0.0%` or another numeric default and present it as authoritative.
- **Four-way equality:** range thumb position, visible numeric value, accessibility value (`aria-valuenow` or equivalent) and mutation/API payload must derive from the same canonical value. After save/refresh/rollback, the returned server value becomes the only displayed authority.
- **Auto mode is visibly read-only:** when automatic balancing owns a parameter, controls cannot appear freely editable. Show applied current value and AI/controller candidate separately. Manual change requires an explicit override/edit action, authorization, reason, reauthentication where required, optimistic version check and rollback metadata.
- **No ambiguous AI trust labels:** model availability/health, review count, calibrated confidence/uncertainty, evidence sufficiency, council agreement and policy eligibility are separate fields. A label such as `average trust 22.5%` is forbidden unless the metric formula, evidence window/sample and operational meaning are visible or directly linked.
- **Real-data hydration QA:** acceptance must exercise initial skeleton -> API hydration -> auto/manual transition -> edit/save -> server reread -> refresh -> rollback/error paths. A visually correct mocked/default state does not prove the control contract.
- **P0 failure:** any stale/default `0.0%`, slider/value disagreement, auto-owned control presented as editable, or undefined confidence/trust percentage blocks Test acceptance and Production promotion.
- This supplements v440 responsive correctness. Detailed authority is `AI_ECONOMY_CONTROLLER_SPEC`. Planning/documentation only; runtime remediation is not claimed.

## P0 administrator mobile/responsive correctness hard gate — v2026.09.25.440 (2026-09-25)

- **Observed defect class:** the Economy Operations administrator surface can exceed the mobile viewport, clip navigation/labels, over-densify AI Council cards, and present control/value layouts that are not reliably readable at narrow widths. These are functional defects, not cosmetic exceptions.

Cards, headings, badges, model names, descriptions, tabs and controls may wrap/reflow but must not be clipped off-screen. One screenshot or one viewport is not acceptance evidence.

## P0 login/session persistence hard gate — v2026.09.25.439 (2026-09-25)

- **User-visible invariant:** an authenticated user whose session is still valid MUST remain signed in across backend/frontend restart, systemd service restart, host reboot, reverse-proxy reload, blue-green/canary cutover, rollback, and routine application deployment. Runtime replacement alone is never a logout reason.
- **Allowed logout reasons are explicit and narrow:** user-requested logout, administrator/security revocation, credential-compromise response, account disable/delete, or normal server-authoritative expiry. Deploy/restart/config reload/key rotation without a security revocation decision is not an allowed reason.
- **Durable authority:** session records and all material needed to validate them must be deployment-independent and durable. Process-local memory may cache auth state but cannot be its sole authority. Restart procedures must not truncate/replace the shared session authority.
- **Key continuity:** signing/encryption key rotation must support overlapping validation of still-valid sessions. Cookie name/domain/path/SameSite/Secure/HttpOnly, issuer/audience and compatible session schema must remain migration-safe across old/new generations.
- **No silent fallback to guest:** a session-validation fault caused by release/config/key/session-store mismatch must surface as a release failure and rollback signal; clients must not quietly treat a valid pre-release user as a guest and ask them to log in again.
- **Mandatory continuity QA:** before restart/cutover capture at least three authenticated sessions covering browser web, API/mobile-compatible auth, and a representative privileged/re-auth flow where applicable. After Test restart and after Production cutover, exercise the same pre-existing sessions without interactive login and verify authenticated viewer/read plus one safe mutation/CSRF flow.
- **Promotion blocker:** any deployment-caused logout, unexpected session loss, auth-key mismatch, cookie incompatibility, or release-attributable 401/403 spike blocks Production promotion or triggers automatic rollback. Passing health checks without session continuity is insufficient.
- **Evidence:** record exact candidate SHA, pre/post runtime identity, session-store health, pre-existing session IDs or privacy-safe hashes, continuity results, auth error deltas, and rollback decision. Session-count equality by itself does not prove continuity.
- **Regression requirement:** restart/cutover continuity tests are mandatory in release automation. A candidate without exact-SHA Test evidence is not Production-eligible.
- This strengthens and supersedes any weaker interpretation of v396 while preserving its legitimate security revocation cases. Planning/documentation only; no new runtime deployment is claimed by v439.

## Disk capacity and release-retention contract — v2026.09.25.438 (2026-09-25)

- **P0 active-release protection:** never delete a release referenced by `production-current`, `test-current`, or any running Production/Test backend/frontend process CWD.
- **P1 bounded retention:** immutable host releases must not grow without limit. Keep the active release plus at least 10 recent rollback-capable releases per environment; additional retention requires an explicit incident/audit/rollback reason.
- **P1 capacity thresholds:** record root/data filesystem bytes and inode usage before/after cleanup. Warn at 70%, block nonessential build/QA artifact growth at 80%, and treat >=90% as an operations incident requiring immediate capacity action.
- **P1 cleanup scope:** stale release copies, package/build caches and explicitly unreferenced container artifacts may be reclaimed; PostgreSQL data, user uploads, backups, active release roots and retain-until-classified QA data are excluded from generic cleanup.
- **P1 swap safety:** disk swap sizing is part of the v437 VM memory-continuity contract. Do not shrink/remove swap solely to free disk without guest/host memory evidence and a rollback plan.
- **Automation:** every successful promotion runs a fail-closed retention job after health/version/session checks. The job protects active CWD/symlink targets, retains the policy window, emits bytes/inodes reclaimed, and aborts on identity ambiguity.
- Detailed authority: [STORAGE_RELEASE_RETENTION_SPEC.md](STORAGE_RELEASE_RETENTION_SPEC.md). Runtime cleanup evidence is recorded separately; this planning version does not redefine application release identity.

## Infrastructure stall resilience and VM crash-continuity contract — v2026.09.25.437 (2026-09-25)

- **P0 hypervisor/guest memory isolation:** Production must have a guaranteed guest memory floor and host reserve. Ballooning/overcommit may not reclaim memory below the empirically safe floor; host memory pressure, PSI, swap, QEMU RSS and guest free/available memory are release/operations signals.
- **P0 multi-layer health:** health authority is composed from external public probe + Nginx/edge + backend + a lightweight DB transaction + guest heartbeat/guest-agent + virtualization-host QEMU state. Application-local health alone cannot certify VM health.
- **P0 stall detection:** alert on repeated `kvm_async_pf`, kernel hung-task/D-state, QEMU pause/reset, guest-agent loss, host OOM, abnormal steal/scheduling delay and sustained storage I/O latency. The response distinguishes app failure from VM/hypervisor failure before remediation.
- **P0 safe remediation:** external watchdog remediation uses explicit duration thresholds, cooldown, maximum retries and fencing. Capture diagnostics first where possible; restart the smallest failing layer first, and only restart/fail over the VM when VM-level evidence justifies it. Reboot storms are prohibited.
- **P0 database recovery ordering:** data filesystem -> PostgreSQL recovery/readiness -> backend -> frontend -> edge acceptance. During WAL/filesystem recovery, dependents back off instead of rapid restart loops. Durable WAL/fsync, verified backup/restore and post-recovery integrity checks are mandatory.
- **P1 resource contention control:** Production has reserved resource capacity. Test builds, browser QA, backups and local AI inference are constrained by CPU/memory/I/O limits or scheduling windows so they cannot starve Production.
- **P1 evidence retention:** retain Proxmox/QEMU task events, host kernel/OOM/PSI/storage telemetry and guest/system/application/DB logs with synchronized timestamps and release SHA, including pre-crash windows.
- **QA/release gate:** fault-inject memory pressure, guest pause/stall and DB crash recovery on Test. Accept only with zero ledger corruption, bounded automatic recovery, correct dependency ordering, external alert evidence, and session continuity when durable session authority survives. Missing host-level telemetry/watchdog blocks Production eligibility.
- Canonical detail: [INFRASTRUCTURE_STALL_RESILIENCE_SPEC.md](INFRASTRUCTURE_STALL_RESILIENCE_SPEC.md). Planning only; no runtime change is claimed by this version.

## 6-Domain Defect Mitigation & Real-Time/Fintech/Security Architecture Spec — v2026.09.23.406 (2026-09-23)

- **P0 LOB WebSocket Monotonic Sequence Gap Recovery (Stocks):** All tick/orderbook broadcasts must carry a monotonic `sequence_id`. On detecting `incoming_seq > last_seq + 1`, clients must discard local state and trigger automatic REST full snapshot resynchronization.
- **P1 KRX 7-Tier Discrete Tick Size (Stocks):** Discrete price steps (1 WLD to 1,000 WLD) are enforced across extreme price ranges (53 WLD to 8.99M WLD).
- **P0 2% Market Transaction Tax & Automated GE Item Sink (Economy):** Combats hyperinflation and item devaluation via a 2% transaction tax (500k WLD cap); 50% is permanently burnt and 50% funds Treasury buybacks of floor-price items for permanent destruction.
- **P0 Client UUID Idempotency & Cursor-Based Pagination (1-on-1 Chat):** Eliminates double-send issues via `(conversation_id, client_message_id)` and prevents message skipping during active conversations via strict `id < cursor` queries.
- **P0 Aave Kinked Jump Rate Model & 20% Statutory Reserve Buffer (Banking):** Prevents bank runs via steep penalty rates (up to 48%) when loan utilization $U > 80\%$, freezing a mandatory 20% reserve buffer for guaranteed withdrawals.
- **P1 7-Day Grace Period Dual-Key Overlap Rotation (Auth):** Guarantees zero session invalidation during secret rotation and zero-downtime blue-green promotions.
- **P1 44px Minimum Touch Target & Safe Area Bottom Insets (UX):** Enforces Apple HIG / WCAG 2.2 AA compliance across 320px to 1280px+ viewports.
- **Authoritative Spec:** [deltas/v2026.09.23.406.md](deltas/v2026.09.23.406.md).
